title.raw: 卷二十七 列傳第十五: 屈遵 張蒲 谷渾 公孫表 張濟 李先 賈彝 竇瑾 李訢 韓延之 袁式 毛脩之 唐和 寇讚 酈範 韓秀 堯暄 柳崇 Volume 27 Biographies 15: Qun Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, Gong Sunbiao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jai Yi, Dou Jin, Li Xin, Han Yanzhi, Yuan Shi, Mao Xiuzhi, Tang He, Kou Zan, Li Fan, Han Xiu, Yao Xuan, Liu Cheng

sentences.zh: 列傳第十五

translations.literal: Biographies 15
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 15

sentences.zh: 屈遵張蒲谷渾曾孫楷公孫表張濟李先賈彝竇瑾李䐶

translations.literal: Qu Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, great-grandson Kai, Gong Sunbiao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jia Yi, Dou Jin, Li Xin
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, great-grandson Kai, Gong Sunbiao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jia Yi, Dou Jin, and Li Xin

sentences.zh: 韓延之袁式毛修之嚴棱硃修之唐和寇贊孫俊酈范子道元韓秀堯暄孫雄柳崇

translations.literal: Han Yanzhi, Yuan Shi, Mao Xiuzhi, Yan Ling, Zhu Xiuzhi, Tang He, Kou Zan, Sun Jun, Li Fan, son Daoyuan, Han Xiu, Yao Xuan, Sun Xiong, Liu Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, Yuan Shi, Mao Xiuzhi, Yan Ling, Zhu Xiuzhi, Tang He, Kou Zan, Sun Jun, Li Fan, son Daoyuan, Han Xiu, Yao Xuan, Sun Xiong, and Liu Cheng

sentences.zh: 屈遵，字子度，昌黎徒何人也。

translations.literal: Qu Zun, styled Zidu, was a native of Tuhé in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zun, styled Zidu, was a native of Tuhé in Changli.

sentences.zh: 博學多才藝。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and skilled in many arts.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and skilled in many arts.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂以為博陸令。

translations.literal: Murong Chui appointed him Bolu Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui appointed him Bolu Commandant.

sentences.zh: 道武南伐，博陵太守申永南奔河外，高陽太守崔宏東走海濱。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu marched south, Boling Administrator Shen Yong fled south across the Yellow River, and Gaoyang Administrator Cui Hong fled east toward the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu marched south, Boling Administrator Shen Yong fled south across the Yellow River, and Gaoyang Administrator Cui Hong fled east toward the sea.

sentences.zh: 屬城長吏，率多逃竄，遵獨歸道武。

translations.literal: Subordinate magistrates for the most part fled or hid; Zun alone came over to Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate magistrates for the most part fled or hid; Zun alone came over to Daowu.

sentences.zh: 道武素聞其名，拜中書令。

translations.literal: Daowu had long heard his name and appointed him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu had long heard his name and appointed him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中原既平，賜爵下蔡子。

translations.literal: After the Central Plains were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiaxia.
translations.idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiaxia.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子須襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Xu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 除長樂太守，進爵信都侯。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Changle and advanced to Marquis of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Changle and advanced to Marquis of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈昌黎公，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Changli with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Changli with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 須長子恆，字長生，沈粹有局量。

translations.literal: Xu's eldest son Heng, styled Changsheng, was deep and pure in character and possessed composure and breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's eldest son Heng, styled Changsheng, was deep and pure in character and possessed composure and breadth of mind.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書右僕射，加侍中。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the additional title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以破平涼功，賜爵濟北公。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Liang Province he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in pacifying Liang Province he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 太武委以大政，車駕出征，常居中留鎮。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu entrusted him with great affairs of state; whenever the imperial carriage went on campaign, he usually remained at the center to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu entrusted him with great affairs of state; whenever the imperial carriage went on campaign, he usually remained at the center to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 與襄城公盧魯元俱賜甲第。

translations.literal: Together with the Duke of Xiangcheng, Lu Luyuan, he was granted a fine mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Duke of Xiangcheng, Lu Luyuan, he was granted a fine mansion.

sentences.zh: 真君四年，墜馬卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenjun he fell from his horse and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenjun he fell from his horse and died.

sentences.zh: 時帝幸陰山，景穆遣使乘傳奏狀。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was at Yinshan; Emperor Jingmu sent a messenger by relay to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was at Yinshan; Emperor Jingmu sent a messenger by relay to report the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悼惜之，謂使人曰：「汝等殺朕良臣，何用乘馬？

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply and said to the messenger, "You have killed my worthy minister—what need is there to ride a horse?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and said to the messenger, "You have killed my worthy minister—what need is there to ride a horse?"

sentences.zh: 」遂令步歸。

translations.literal: He then ordered him to return on foot.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered him to return on foot.

sentences.zh: 贈征西大將軍，諡曰成公。

translations.literal: Heng was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West, with the posthumous name Duke Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West, with the posthumous name Duke Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子道賜襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Daoci inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoci inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 道賜善騎射，機辯有辭氣，太武甚器之。

translations.literal: Daoci was skilled at riding and archery, quick-witted and eloquent; Taiwu greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoci was skilled at riding and archery, quick-witted and eloquent; Taiwu greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 位尚書右僕射，加侍中。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the additional title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰哀公。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Duke Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Duke Ai.

sentences.zh: 子拔襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Ba inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ba inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 帝追思其父祖，年十四，以為南部大人。

translations.literal: The emperor, recalling his father and grandfather, at age fourteen made him Grand Warden of the Southern Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, recalling his father and grandfather, at age fourteen made him Grand Warden of the Southern Tribes.

sentences.zh: 時太武南伐，禽守將胡盛之以付拔。

translations.literal: When Taiwu campaigned south he captured the defending general Hu Shengzhi and handed him over to Ba.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu campaigned south he captured the defending general Hu Shengzhi and handed him over to Ba.

sentences.zh: 酒醉不覺，盛之逃。

translations.literal: Drunk, Ba did not notice; Shengzhi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Ba did not notice; Shengzhi escaped.

sentences.zh: 太武令斬之。

translations.literal: Taiwu ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 將伏鑕，帝愴然曰：「若鬼有知，長生問其子孫，朕將何以應？

translations.literal: As he was about to face the axe, the emperor said sorrowfully, "If ghosts have awareness, when Changsheng asks his descendants what answer shall I give?"
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to face the axe, the emperor said sorrowfully, "If ghosts have awareness, when Changsheng asks his descendants what answer shall I give?"

sentences.zh: 」乃赦拔。

translations.literal: He then pardoned Ba.
translations.idiomatic: He then pardoned Ba.

sentences.zh: 後獻文以其功臣子，拜營州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xianwen, as the son of a meritorious minister, appointed him Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xianwen, as the son of a meritorious minister, appointed him Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 張蒲，字玄則，河內修武人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Pu, styled Xuanze, was a native of Xiuwu in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu, styled Xuanze, was a native of Xiuwu in Henei.

sentences.zh: 本名謨。

translations.literal: His original name was Mo.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Mo.

sentences.zh: 父攀，仕慕容垂，位兵部尚書，以清方稱。

translations.literal: His father Pan served Murong Chui as Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was known for integrity and rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pan served Murong Chui as Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was known for integrity and rectitude.

sentences.zh: 蒲少有父風，仕慕容寶為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Pu in youth had his father's bearing and served Murong Bao as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pu in youth had his father's bearing and served Murong Bao as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 道武定中山，寶官司敘用，多降品秩。

translations.literal: When Daowu pacified Zhongshan, Bao's officials were reassigned for service, and many were demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu pacified Zhongshan, Bao's officials were reassigned for service, and many were demoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 帝既素聞蒲名，仍拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: The emperor had long heard Pu's name and still appointed him Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long heard Pu's name and still appointed him Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，為內都大官，賜爵泰昌子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan acceded, he became Grand Director of the Inner Court and was enfeoffed as Baron of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan acceded, he became Grand Director of the Inner Court and was enfeoffed as Baron of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 參決庶獄，私謁不行。

translations.literal: He took part in deciding ordinary legal cases, and private petitions were not entertained.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in deciding ordinary legal cases, and private petitions were not entertained.

sentences.zh: 後改為壽張子。

translations.literal: Later his title was changed to Baron of Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was changed to Baron of Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 太武即位，以蒲清貧，妻子衣食不給，乃以為相州刺史。

translations.literal: When Taiwu acceded, because Pu was poor and his wife and children lacked adequate food and clothing, he was made Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu acceded, because Pu was poor and his wife and children lacked adequate food and clothing, he was made Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 扶弱抑強，進善黜惡，風化大行。

translations.literal: He supported the weak and restrained the strong, promoted the good and dismissed the evil, and moral transformation flourished widely.
translations.idiomatic: He supported the weak and restrained the strong, promoted the good and dismissed the evil, and moral transformation flourished widely.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，吏人痛惜之。

translations.literal: He died in office; officials and commoners grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; officials and commoners grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 蒲在謀臣之列，屢出為將，朝廷論之，常以為稱首。

translations.literal: Pu stood among the strategists and was repeatedly sent out as a general; whenever the court discussed him, he was always spoken of as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Pu stood among the strategists and was repeatedly sent out as a general; whenever the court discussed him, he was always spoken of as foremost.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、廣平公，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Guangping, with the posthumous name Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Guangping, with the posthumous name Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子昭襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao inherited.

sentences.zh: 以軍功進爵修武侯，位幽州刺史，以善政見稱。

translations.literal: For military merit he was advanced to Marquis of Xiuyang and made Governor of Youzhou, famed for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was advanced to Marquis of Xiuyang and made Governor of Youzhou, famed for good governance.

sentences.zh: 穀渾，字元沖，昌黎人也。

translations.literal: Gu Hun, styled Yuanchong, was a native of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Hun, styled Yuanchong, was a native of Changli.

sentences.zh: 父袞，彎弓三百斤，勇冠一時。

translations.literal: His father Gun could draw a three-hundred-jin bow and was the bravest man of his age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gun could draw a three-hundred-jin bow and was the bravest man of his age.

sentences.zh: 仕慕容垂，位廣武將軍。

translations.literal: He served Murong Chui as General of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Chui as General of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 渾少有父風，任俠好氣，晚乃折節受經業，被服類儒者。

translations.literal: Hun in youth had his father's spirit, was chivalrous and spirited; only later did he restrain himself and take up classical studies, dressing like a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Hun in youth had his father's spirit, was chivalrous and spirited; only later did he restrain himself and take up classical studies, dressing like a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 道武時，以善隸書為內侍左右。

translations.literal: In Daowu's time, because he excelled at clerical script he served in the inner attendants at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: In Daowu's time, because he excelled at clerical script he served in the inner attendants at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 太武時，累遷侍中、儀曹尚書，賜爵濮陽公。

translations.literal: Under Taiwu he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Bureau of Rites, and enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiwu he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Bureau of Rites, and enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 渾正直有操行，性不苟合。

translations.literal: Hun was upright and possessed moral conduct; by nature he did not curry favor casually.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was upright and possessed moral conduct; by nature he did not curry favor casually.

sentences.zh: 然愛重舊故，不以富貴驕人，時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: Yet he cherished old friends and did not look down on others because of wealth or rank; people of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cherished old friends and did not look down on others because of wealth or rank; people of the time praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 在官廉直，為太武所器重。

translations.literal: In office he was incorrupt and direct, and Taiwu valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was incorrupt and direct, and Taiwu valued him.

sentences.zh: 以渾子孫年十五以上，悉補中書學生。

translations.literal: Because Hun's sons and grandsons were fifteen or older, all were enrolled as students of the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hun's sons and grandsons were fifteen or older, all were enrolled as students of the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子闡，字崇基，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chan, styled Chongji, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chan, styled Chongji, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 位外都大官。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Grand Director of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the post of Grand Director of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡公。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Duke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Duke Jian.

sentences.zh: 子洪，字元孫，位尚書，賜爵滎陽公。

translations.literal: His son Hong, styled Yuansun, reached the post of Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong, styled Yuansun, reached the post of Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 性貪奢，僕妾衣服錦綺。

translations.literal: By nature greedy and extravagant, his servants and concubines wore brocade and fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: By nature greedy and extravagant, his servants and concubines wore brocade and fine silk.

sentences.zh: 時獻文舅李峻等初至，官給衣服，洪輒截沒。

translations.literal: At the time Xianwen's maternal uncle Li Jun and others had just arrived; the government supplied clothing, and Hong intercepted and kept it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xianwen's maternal uncle Li Jun and others had just arrived; the government supplied clothing, and Hong intercepted and kept it.

sentences.zh: 為有司所糾，並窮其前後贓罪，伏法。

translations.literal: Impeached by the relevant office, his past and present corrupt acts were fully investigated, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached by the relevant office, his past and present corrupt acts were fully investigated, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 子穎，位太府少卿。

translations.literal: His son Ying held the post of Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying held the post of Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈營州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Yingzhou with the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Yingzhou with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子士恢，字紹達，位鴻臚少卿，封元城縣侯。

translations.literal: His son Shihui, styled Shaoda, was Vice Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shihui, styled Shaoda, was Vice Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 太后嬖幸鄭儼，懼紹達間構於帝，因言次，以紹達為州。

translations.literal: The empress dowager favored Zheng Yan and feared Shaoda would sow discord with the emperor; on a casual occasion she had Shaoda sent out to a province.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager favored Zheng Yan and feared Shaoda would sow discord with the emperor; on a casual occasion she had Shaoda sent out to a province.

sentences.zh: 紹達耽寵，不願出。

translations.literal: Shaoda was infatuated with favor and unwilling to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoda was infatuated with favor and unwilling to leave.

sentences.zh: 太后誣其罪，殺之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager fabricated charges against him and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager fabricated charges against him and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 渾曾孫楷。

translations.literal: Hun's great-great-grandson Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's great-great-grandson Kai.

sentences.zh: 楷有幹局，稍遷奉車都尉。

translations.literal: Kai had ability and foresight and was gradually promoted to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Kai had ability and foresight and was gradually promoted to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 眇一目，性甚嚴忍，前後奉使皆以酷暴為名，時人號曰「瞎武」。

translations.literal: Blind in one eye and by nature very stern and cruel, on missions before and after he was known for violence; people of the time called him "Blind Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Blind in one eye and by nature very stern and cruel, on missions before and after he was known for violence; people of the time called him "Blind Wu."

sentences.zh: 累遷城門校尉，卒。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Commandant of the City Gates and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Commandant of the City Gates and died.

sentences.zh: 公孫表，字玄元，燕郡廣陽人也。

translations.literal: Gong Sunbiao, styled Xuanyuan, was a native of Guangyang in Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sunbiao, styled Xuanyuan, was a native of Guangyang in Yan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 為慕容沖尚書郎。

translations.literal: He served Murong Chong as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Chong as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂破長子，從入中山。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui took Changzi, Biao followed him into Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui took Changzi, Biao followed him into Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶走，乃歸，為博士。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao fled, he submitted and was made a Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao fled, he submitted and was made a Erudite.

sentences.zh: 初，道武以慕容垂諸子分據勢要，權柄推移，遂至亡滅，表詣闕上《韓非書》二十卷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Daowu had seen how Murong Chui's sons each held strategic posts and power shifted until ruin came; Biao went to court and presented twenty scrolls of Han Feizi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Daowu had seen how Murong Chui's sons each held strategic posts and power shifted until ruin came; Biao went to court and presented twenty scrolls of Han Feizi.

sentences.zh: 道武稱善。

translations.literal: Daowu praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu praised it.

sentences.zh: 明元初，賜爵固安子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingyuan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Mingyuan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 河西饑胡劉武反於上黨，詔表討之。

translations.literal: The starving Hu of Hexi, Liu Wu, rebelled at Shangdang; an edict ordered Biao to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The starving Hu of Hexi, Liu Wu, rebelled at Shangdang; an edict ordered Biao to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 為胡所敗，帝深銜之。

translations.literal: He was defeated by the Hu; the emperor bore a deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated by the Hu; the emperor bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 泰常七年，宋武帝殂。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang, Emperor Wu of Song died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taichang, Emperor Wu of Song died.

sentences.zh: 時議取河南侵地，以奚斤為都督，以表為吳兵將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time the court debated taking the invaded lands south of the Yellow River; Xi Jin was made supreme commander, and Biao was made General of Wu Troops and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated taking the invaded lands south of the Yellow River; Xi Jin was made supreme commander, and Biao was made General of Wu Troops and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 表既克滑台，遂圍武牢。

translations.literal: After Biao took Huatai, he then besieged Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: After Biao took Huatai, he then besieged Wulao.

sentences.zh: 車駕次汲郡。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage halted at Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 始昌子蘇坦、太史令王亮奏表置軍武牢東，不得形便之地，故令賊不時滅。

translations.literal: Shichangzi Su Tan and Grand Astrologer Wang Liang memorialized that Biao had placed his army east of Wulao, not on advantageous ground, and so the bandits were not destroyed in time.
translations.idiomatic: Shichangzi Su Tan and Grand Astrologer Wang Liang memorialized that Biao had placed his army east of Wulao, not on advantageous ground, and so the bandits were not destroyed in time.

sentences.zh: 明元雅好術數，又積前忿，及攻武牢，士卒多傷，乃使人夜就帳中縊殺之。

translations.literal: Mingyuan was fond of numerology and divination and still harbored old resentment; when the assault on Wulao cost many wounded soldiers, he sent men at night into the tent to strangle Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan was fond of numerology and divination and still harbored old resentment; when the assault on Wulao cost many wounded soldiers, he sent men at night into the tent to strangle Biao.

sentences.zh: 以賊未退，秘而不宣。

translations.literal: Because the enemy had not yet withdrawn, it was kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Because the enemy had not yet withdrawn, it was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 初，表與勃海封愷友善，後為子求愷從女，愷不許，表甚銜之。

translations.literal: Earlier Biao had been on friendly terms with Feng Kai of Bohai; later he sought Kai's niece by marriage for his son, and Kai refused—Biao resented it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Biao had been on friendly terms with Feng Kai of Bohai; later he sought Kai's niece by marriage for his son, and Kai refused—Biao resented it deeply.

sentences.zh: 及封氏為司馬國璠所逮，帝以舊族，欲原之。

translations.literal: When the Feng clan was seized by Sima Guofan, the emperor wished to pardon them as an old family.
translations.idiomatic: When the Feng clan was seized by Sima Guofan, the emperor wished to pardon them as an old family.

sentences.zh: 表證其罪，乃誅封氏。

translations.literal: Biao proved their guilt, and the Feng clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Biao proved their guilt, and the Feng clan was executed.

sentences.zh: 表外和內忌，時人以此薄之。

translations.literal: Outwardly harmonious yet inwardly jealous—people of the time despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly cordial yet inwardly envious—contemporaries looked down on him for it.

sentences.zh: 表本與王亮同營署，及其出也，輕侮亮，故及於死。

translations.literal: Biao had originally shared an office with Wang Liang; when he went out on campaign he treated Liang lightly, and so came to his death.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had once shared an office with Wang Liang; when he took the field on campaign he slighted Liang, and that was how he met his end.

sentences.zh: 第二子軌，字元慶。

translations.literal: His second son Gui, styled Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Gui, styled Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 明元時，為中書郎。

translations.literal: In Mingyuan's time he was a Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingyuan's time he was a Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 出從征討，補諸軍司馬。

translations.literal: Going out on campaigns, he was made staff officer to the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he served as staff officer to the various armies.

sentences.zh: 太武平赫連昌，引諸將帥入其府藏，各令任意取金玉。

translations.literal: When Taiwu pacified Helian Chang, he led the generals into the treasury and let each take gold and jade at will.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu conquered Helian Chang, he brought the generals into the state treasury and allowed each to help himself to gold and jade as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 諸將取之盈懷，軌獨不取。

translations.literal: The generals filled their bosoms; Gui alone took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The generals stuffed their robes full; Gui alone took nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝把手親探金賜之，謂曰：「卿臨財廉，朕所以增賜者，欲顯廉於眾人。

translations.literal: The emperor took gold in hand and gave it to him personally, saying, "You are incorruptible before wealth—that is why I add to your gift: I wish to display integrity before the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took gold in his hand and gave it to him in person, saying, "You are incorruptible in the face of wealth—that is why I add to your gift: I wish to show the multitude what integrity looks like."

sentences.zh: 」後兼大鴻臚，持節拜立氐楊玄為南秦王。

translations.literal: Later he also served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and, bearing credentials, invested the Di leader Yang Xuan as King of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He later also held the post of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and, bearing credentials, invested the Di chieftain Yang Xuan as King of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 及境，玄不郊迎；

translations.literal: At the border Xuan did not come out to meet him in the suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the border, Xuan did not come out to the suburbs to greet him;

sentences.zh: 軌數玄無蕃臣禮。

translations.literal: Gui repeatedly reproached Xuan for lacking the rites due a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Gui again and again rebuked Xuan for failing to observe the rites owed a vassal.

sentences.zh: 玄懼，詣郊受命。

translations.literal: Xuan feared him and went to the suburbs to receive the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Gui, Xuan went to the suburbs to accept the investiture.

sentences.zh: 使還稱旨，拜尚書，賜爵燕郡公，出為武牢鎮將。

translations.literal: On his return his mission was deemed satisfactory; he was made Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan Commandery, and sent out as garrison commander of Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, his mission was judged satisfactory; he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan Commandery, and sent out as garrison commander of Wulao.

sentences.zh: 初，太武將北征，發驢以運糧，使軌部調雍州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Taiwu was about to campaign north, donkeys were levied to transport grain, and Gui was ordered to coordinate them in Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Taiwu was preparing a northern campaign, donkeys were conscripted to haul grain, and Gui was ordered to organize the levy in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 軌令驢主皆加絹一匹，乃與受之。

translations.literal: Gui ordered that each donkey-owner receive an extra bolt of silk before the animals were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Gui ordered that each owner of a donkey be given an extra bolt of silk before the animal was taken.

sentences.zh: 百姓語曰：「驢無強弱，輔脊自壯。

translations.literal: The people said, "Donkeys have no weak or strong—the pack-saddle makes them stout."
translations.idiomatic: The people said, "Donkeys are neither weak nor strong—the pack-saddle is what makes them look stout."

sentences.zh: 」眾共嗤之。

translations.literal: Everyone mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone mocked him.

sentences.zh: 坐征還。

translations.literal: He was recalled for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled for investigation.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 軌既死，帝謂崔浩曰：「吾過上黨，父老皆曰：公孫軌為將，受貨縱賊，使至今餘奸不除，軌之罪也。

translations.literal: After Gui died the emperor said to Cui Hao, "When I passed Shangdang the elders all said, 'Gong Sun Gui as a general took bribes and let bandits go, so that evildoers remain to this day—that is Gui's crime.'"
translations.idiomatic: After Gui died the emperor said to Cui Hao, "When I passed through Shangdang the elders all said, 'Gong Sun Gui as a general took bribes and let bandits go free, so that evildoers remain to this day—that is Gui's crime.'"

sentences.zh: 其初來，單馬執鞭；

translations.literal: When he first came, a single horse and whip in hand;
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived, he came alone with a single horse and whip in hand;

sentences.zh: 及去，從車百兩。

translations.literal: when he left, a train of a hundred carts followed.
translations.idiomatic: when he left, a train of a hundred carts followed.

sentences.zh: 載物而南，丁零渠帥，乘山罵軌。

translations.literal: Loaded with goods he went south; a Dingling chieftain on the mountain cursed Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing a load of goods, he went south; a Dingling chieftain on the mountainside cursed Gui.

sentences.zh: 軌怒，取罵軌者之母，以矛刺其陰而死之，曰：'何以生此逆子！

translations.literal: Gui in anger took the curser's mother and stabbed her privates to death, saying, 'Why bear such a rebellious son!'
translations.idiomatic: When Gui flew into a rage he seized the curser's mother and stabbed her private parts to death, crying, "Why give birth to such a rebellious son!"

sentences.zh: '從下倒劈，分磔四支於山樹上。

translations.literal: From below he split her body downward and hung the four limbs on mountain trees.
translations.idiomatic: He split her body open from below and hung her four limbs on mountain trees.

sentences.zh: 是忍行不忍之事。

translations.literal: Such cruelty toward what mercy forbids.
translations.idiomatic: Such cruelty toward what mercy forbids.

sentences.zh: 軌幸而早死，至今在者，吾必族誅之。」

translations.literal: Gui was fortunate to die early; had he still lived, I would have exterminated his clan."
translations.idiomatic: Gui was lucky to have died young; had he still been alive, I would have wiped out his entire clan."

sentences.zh: 軌終得娶封氏，生子睿，字叔文。

translations.literal: Gui finally married into the Feng clan and begot Rui, styled Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Gui married into the Feng clan and fathered Rui, styled Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 位儀曹長，賜爵陽平公。

translations.literal: He reached Director of the Bureau of Rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Bureau of Rites and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 時獻文于苑內立殿，敕中秘群官制名。

translations.literal: When Xianwen built a hall in the park, he ordered the secretariat officials to devise a name.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianwen built a hall in the imperial park, he ordered the Secretariat officials to propose a name for it.

sentences.zh: 睿奏曰：「臣聞至尊至貴，莫崇於帝王；

translations.literal: Rui memorialized, "I have heard that nothing is more honored than the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Rui submitted a memorial: "I have heard that nothing is more exalted than the emperor;

sentences.zh: 天人挹損，莫大于謙光。

translations.literal: nothing greater than modest light withheld between Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: and nothing greater than the modest restraint kept between Heaven and man."

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜曰崇光。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and thinks it should be called Chongguang."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is dull-witted and believes it should be named Chongguang."

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 卒于南部尚書，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died as Director of the Southern Masters of Writing, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Director of the Southern Masters of Writing; his posthumous name was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 睿妻，崔浩弟女也。

translations.literal: Rui's wife was a daughter of Cui Hao's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Rui married a daughter of Cui Hao's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 生子良，字遵伯，聰明好學。

translations.literal: She bore Liang, styled Zunbo, clever and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: She gave birth to Liang, styled Zunbo, who was clever and fond of learning.

sentences.zh: 為尚書左丞，為孝文所知遇。

translations.literal: He was Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and won Emperor Xiaowen's favor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and won the esteem of Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 良弟衡，字道津。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Heng, styled Daojin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's younger brother Heng, styled Daojin.

sentences.zh: 良推爵讓之，仕至司直。

translations.literal: Liang yielded his title to him; Heng rose to Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Liang yielded his rank to him; Heng rose to become Director of Justice.

sentences.zh: 良以別功，賜爵昌平子。

translations.literal: For separate merit Liang was enfeoffed as Baron of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: For his own separate merit Liang was enfeoffed as Baron of Changping.

sentences.zh: 子崇基襲。

translations.literal: His son Chongji inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongji inherited.

sentences.zh: 軌弟質，字元直，有經義，為中書學生，稍遷博士。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Zhi, styled Yuanzhi, versed in the classics, was a student of the Secretariat Academy and was gradually promoted to Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Zhi, styled Yuanzhi, versed in the classics, entered the Secretariat Academy as a student and was gradually promoted to Erudite.

sentences.zh: 太武征涼州，留宜都王穆壽輔景穆。

translations.literal: When Taiwu campaigned against Liangzhou, he left Prince Yidu Mu Shou to assist Jingmu.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu marched against Liangzhou, he left Prince Yidu Mu Shou behind to assist Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 時蠕蠕乘虛犯塞，京師震恐。

translations.literal: At the time the Rouran exploited the opening to raid the frontier; the capital was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Rouran seized the opportunity to raid the borderlands; the capital trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 壽雅信任質，為謀主。

translations.literal: Shou greatly trusted Zhi and made him chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Shou placed great trust in Zhi and made him his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 質性好卜筮；

translations.literal: Zhi was fond of divination;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was fond of divination;

sentences.zh: 卜筮者咸雲必不來，故不設備。

translations.literal: the diviners all said the enemy would certainly not come, and so no preparations were made.
translations.idiomatic: All the diviners declared that the enemy would surely not come, and so no defensive measures were taken.

sentences.zh: 由質，幾敗國。

translations.literal: Because of Zhi the state nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Zhi the state nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 後屢進讜言，超遷尚書。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly offered forthright counsel and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he repeatedly offered blunt counsel and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈廣陽侯，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Marquis of Guangyang with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangyang with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 第二子邃，字文慶，位南部尚書，封襄平伯，出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: His second son Sui, styled Wenqing, was Director of the Southern Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangping, and sent out as Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Sui, styled Wenqing, became Director of the Southern Masters of Writing, was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangping, and was sent out as Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以邃在公遺跡可紀，下詔褒述。

translations.literal: Because Sui's public legacy was worth recording, an edict praised and recounted it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sui's record of public service was worth preserving, an edict commended and recounted his deeds.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 孝文在鄴宮，為之舉哀。

translations.literal: Xiaowen was at the palace in Ye and held mourning for him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was at the palace in Ye and observed mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 時百度唯新，青州佐吏疑為邃服，詔曰：「專古也，理與今違；

translations.literal: At the time every observance was being renewed; Qingzhou's clerks doubted mourning for Sui, and an edict said, "To follow antiquity alone runs counter to the present;
translations.idiomatic: At the time every observance was being renewed; Qingzhou's clerks doubted whether mourning was due for Sui, and an edict said, "To follow antiquity alone runs counter to the present;

sentences.zh: 專今也，太乖曩義。

translations.literal: to follow the present alone departs too far from former rites.
translations.idiomatic: to follow the present alone departs too far from the rites of old."

sentences.zh: 當斟酌兩途，商量得失，人吏之情亦不可苟順也。

translations.literal: One must weigh both paths and calculate gain and loss—the feelings of officials and clerks cannot be indulged rashly either."
translations.idiomatic: One must weigh both courses and calculate gain and loss—the feelings of officials and clerks cannot be indulged rashly either."

sentences.zh: 主簿雲，近代相承服斬，過葬便，可如故。

translations.literal: The chief clerk said that in recent generations the custom was to wear unhemmed hemp and, once the burial was past, to stop—this might stand as before.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk said that in recent generations the custom was to wear unhemmed hemp and, once the burial was over, to stop mourning—this might stand as before.

sentences.zh: 自餘無服，大成寥落。

translations.literal: For the rest, no mourning—a great void in observance.
translations.idiomatic: For everything else, no mourning—a great void in ritual observance.

sentences.zh: 可准諸境內之人，為齊衰三月。

translations.literal: Let it be permitted that people within the borders wear hemmed mourning for three months."
translations.idiomatic: People within the borders may be allowed to wear hemmed mourning for three months."

sentences.zh: 」子同始襲爵，卒於給事中。

translations.literal: His son Tongshi inherited the title and died as Supervisor in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tongshi inherited the title and later died while serving as Supervisor in the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 邃、睿為從父兄弟。

translations.literal: Sui and Rui were cousins.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and Rui were cousins.

sentences.zh: 睿才器小優，又封氏之男，崔氏之婿。

translations.literal: Rui's talent was slightly the better, and he was a Feng on his mother's side and a Cui by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's talent was slightly the finer, and he was a Feng through his mother and a Cui by marriage.

sentences.zh: 邃母雁門李氏，地望懸隔。

translations.literal: Sui's mother was Li of Yanmen—a family standing far apart in prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's mother was of the Li clan of Yanmen—a family whose standing was worlds apart in prestige.

sentences.zh: 钜鹿太守祖季真多識北方人物，每云：「士大夫當須好婚親。

translations.literal: Julu Administrator Zu Jizhen knew many figures of the north and often said, "A scholar-official must marry well."
translations.idiomatic: Julu Administrator Zu Jizhen knew many notables of the north and would often say, "A scholar-official must make a good marriage."

sentences.zh: 二公孫同堂兄弟耳，吉凶會集，便有士庶之異。」

translations.literal: The two Gong Suns are cousins under one roof—yet when fortune and misfortune gather, the difference between gentry and commoners appears."
translations.idiomatic: The two Gong Suns are cousins under the same roof—yet when fortune and misfortune meet, the gulf between gentry and commoners stands plain."

sentences.zh: 張濟，字士度，西河人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, styled Shidu, was a native of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, styled Shidu, was a native of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 父千秋，慕容永驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Qianqiu was Murong Yong's valiant cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qianqiu had been Murong Yong's valiant cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 永滅，來奔。

translations.literal: When Yong was destroyed, he came over.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong was destroyed, he came over.

sentences.zh: 道武善之，拜建節將軍，賜爵成紀侯。

translations.literal: Daowu treated him well, made him General Who Establishes Discipline, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu received him kindly, appointed him General Who Establishes Discipline, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chengji.

sentences.zh: 濟涉獵書傳，清辯善儀容。

translations.literal: Ji ranged widely in books and records, was clear in debate and graceful in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Ji ranged broadly through books and records, was sharp in debate and graceful in bearing.

sentences.zh: 道武愛之，與公孫表等俱為行人，拜散騎侍郎，襲爵。

translations.literal: Daowu favored him; together with Gong Sunbiao and others he served as envoy, was made Gentleman of the Unattached Cavalry, and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu favored him; together with Gong Sunbiao and others he served as envoy, was appointed Gentleman of the Unattached Cavalry, and inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉雍州刺史楊佺期乞師于常山王遵以禦姚興。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin's Governor of Yong Province Yang Quanqi had asked the Prince of Changshan Zun for troops against Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jin's Governor of Yong Province, Yang Quanqi, had asked the Prince of Changshan, Zun, for troops to resist Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 帝遣濟為遵從事，即報之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Ji as staff to Zun to deliver the reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Ji on Zun's staff to deliver the reply.

sentences.zh: 濟自襄陽還，帝問濟江南事。

translations.literal: Ji returned from Xiangyang; the emperor asked him about affairs south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji returned from Xiangyang, the emperor questioned him about affairs south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「司馬昌明死，子德宗代立，君弱臣強，全無綱紀。

translations.literal: Ji said, "Sima Changming is dead; his son Degong has succeeded. The ruler is young and the ministers strong—there is no discipline at all."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Sima Changming is dead and his son Degong has succeeded. The ruler is young and the ministers are strong—there is no order at all."

sentences.zh: 佺期問臣：'魏初伐中山，幾十萬眾？

translations.literal: Quanqi asked me, 'When Wei first attacked Zhongshan, how many tens of thousands were there?'
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi asked me, "When Wei first attacked Zhongshan, how many tens of thousands of men were there?"

sentences.zh: '臣答：'四十餘萬。

translations.literal: I answered, 'More than four hundred thousand.'
translations.idiomatic: I answered, 'More than four hundred thousand.'

sentences.zh: '佺期曰：'魏被甲戎馬，可有幾匹？

translations.literal: Quanqi said, 'How many armored war-horses does Wei have?'
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi said, "How many armored war-horses does Wei possess?"

sentences.zh: '臣答：'中軍精騎十餘萬，外軍無數。

translations.literal: I answered, 'The central army has more than a hundred thousand elite cavalry; the outer armies are beyond counting.'
translations.idiomatic: I answered, "The central army has more than a hundred thousand elite cavalry; the outer armies are beyond counting."

sentences.zh: '佺期曰：'以此討羌，豈不滅也！

translations.literal: Quanqi said, 'With that force, to chastise the Qiang—would they not be destroyed!'
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi said, "With a force like that, to chastise the Qiang—would they not be utterly destroyed!"

sentences.zh: '又曰：'魏定中山，徙幾戶於北？

translations.literal: He also asked, 'When Wei pacified Zhongshan, how many households were moved north?'
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "When Wei pacified Zhongshan, how many households were relocated north?"

sentences.zh: '臣答：'七萬餘家。

translations.literal: I answered, 'More than seventy thousand families.'
translations.idiomatic: I answered, 'More than seventy thousand families.'

sentences.zh: '佺期曰：'都何城？

translations.literal: Quanqi asked, 'What city was the capital?'
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi asked, 'What city was the capital?'

sentences.zh: '臣答：'都平城。

translations.literal: I answered, 'The capital was Pingcheng.'
translations.idiomatic: I answered, 'The capital was Pingcheng.'

sentences.zh: '佺期曰：' 有此大眾，何用城為！

translations.literal: Quanqi said, 'With such a multitude, what need of walls!'
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi said, "With so vast a multitude, what need is there of city walls!"

sentences.zh: '又曰：'魏帝欲為久都平城？

translations.literal: He also asked, 'Does the Wei emperor mean to make Pingcheng his capital for long,
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "Does the Wei emperor intend to keep Pingcheng as his capital long,

sentences.zh: 將移也？

translations.literal: or will he move?'
translations.idiomatic: or will he move?'

sentences.zh: '臣答：'非所知也。

translations.literal: I answered, 'I do not know.'
translations.idiomatic: I answered, 'I do not know.'

sentences.zh: '佺期聞朝廷不都山東，貌有喜色，曰：'洛城救援，仰恃于魏，若獲保全，當必厚報。

translations.literal: Quanqi heard that the court did not intend to settle east of the mountains and looked pleased, saying, 'Relief for Luoyang depends on Wei; if we can be preserved, we shall surely repay you richly.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi heard that the court did not intend to settle east of the mountains and looked pleased, saying, "Relief for Luoyang depends on Wei; if we can be preserved, we shall surely repay you richly.

sentences.zh: 如為羌所乘，甯使魏取。

translations.literal: If the Qiang should prevail, better let Wei take it.'"
translations.idiomatic: If the Qiang should prevail, better let Wei take it."

sentences.zh: '」道武嘉其辭，厚賞其使，許救洛陽。

translations.literal: Daowu praised his report, richly rewarded the envoy, and promised to rescue Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu commended his report, richly rewarded the envoy, and pledged to rescue Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後以累使稱旨，拜勝兵將軍。

translations.literal: Later, because repeated missions pleased the throne, he was made General of Victorious Troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his repeated missions met with imperial approval, he was appointed General of Victorious Troops.

sentences.zh: 卒，子多羅襲爵，坐事除。

translations.literal: He died; his son Duoluo inherited the title and was stripped of rank for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Duoluo inherited the title but was stripped of rank for an offense.

sentences.zh: 李先，字容仁，中山盧奴人。

translations.literal: Li Xian, styled Rongren, was a native of Lunu in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, styled Rongren, came from Lunu in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善占相術。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled in physiognomy and divination.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he loved learning and was skilled in physiognomy and divination.

sentences.zh: 慕容永迎為謀主，勸永據長子城。

translations.literal: Murong Yong welcomed him as strategist and urged Yong to hold Changzi city.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong welcomed him as strategist and urged Yong to hold the city of Changzi.

sentences.zh: 仕永，位秘書監。

translations.literal: He served Yong as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yong as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永滅，徙中山。

translations.literal: When Yong was destroyed, he was moved to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong's fall, he was relocated to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，先于井陘歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi, Xian submitted at Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huangshi era, Xian came in and submitted at Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 道武問先曰：「卿何國人？

translations.literal: Daowu asked Xian, "Of what state are you a subject?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu asked Xian, "What state do you serve?"

sentences.zh: 祖父及身悉曆何官？

translations.literal: What offices did your grandfather and you yourself hold?"
translations.idiomatic: "What offices did your grandfather hold, and what have you yourself held?"

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「臣本趙郡平棘人。

translations.literal: Xian said, "Your servant is originally from Pingji in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Your servant is a man of Pingji in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 大父重，晉平陽太守、大將軍右司馬。

translations.literal: My great-grandfather Chong was Jin's Administrator of Pingyang and Right Marshal of the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: My great-grandfather Chong served Jin as Administrator of Pingyang and as Right Marshal to the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 父懋，石季龍樂安太守、左中郎將。

translations.literal: My father Mao was Shile's Administrator of Le'an and Left Commandant of the Center.
translations.idiomatic: My father Mao held Shile's post of Administrator of Le'an and served as Left Commandant of the Center.

sentences.zh: 臣，苻丕左主客郎，慕容永秘書監、高密侯。

translations.literal: Your servant was Fu Pi's Left Master of Guests, Murong Yong's Director of the Secretariat, and Marquis of Gaomi."
translations.idiomatic: As for myself, I was Fu Pi's Left Master of Guests, Murong Yong's Director of the Secretariat, and Marquis of Gaomi."

sentences.zh: 」車駕還代，以先為尚書右中兵郎。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Dai, Xian was made Right Gentleman of the Central Guard in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to Dai, Xian was appointed Right Gentleman of the Central Guard in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再遷博士、定州大中正。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Erudite and Grand Rectifier of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Erudite and Grand Rectifier of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 帝問先：「何者最善，可以益人神智？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Xian, "What is best and can augment a ruler's wisdom?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Xian, "What is the finest thing for sharpening a ruler's mind?"

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「唯有經書，三皇、五帝政化之典，可以補王者神智。

translations.literal: Xian said, "Only the classics—the governmental canons of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors—can supplement a king's wisdom."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Only the classics—the governmental canons of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors—can truly supplement a king's wisdom."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「朕欲集天下書籍，如何？

translations.literal: He also asked, "I wish to gather the books of the realm—how should I proceed?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "I wish to collect all the books in the empire—how should I go about it?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「主之所好，集亦不難。

translations.literal: He answered, "What the lord favors is not hard to assemble."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Whatever the lord favors is not hard to bring together."

sentences.zh: 」帝於是班制天下，經籍稍集。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued orders throughout the realm, and the classics gradually accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued orders throughout the realm, and the canonical texts gradually piled up.

sentences.zh: 道武討姚興于柴壁也，問計於先。

translations.literal: When Daowu attacked Yao Xing at Chaibi he sought Xian's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu attacked Yao Xing at Chaibi, he sought Xian's counsel.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「兵以正合，戰以奇勝。

translations.literal: Xian answered, "In war the orthodox joins battle; victory comes through the unexpected."
translations.idiomatic: Xian answered, "In war one meets the enemy in the orthodox way; victory comes by the unexpected."

sentences.zh: 聞姚興欲屯兵天渡，利其糧道。

translations.literal: I hear Yao Xing intends to encamp at Tiandu and profit from his grain route.
translations.idiomatic: "I hear Yao Xing plans to encamp at Tiandu and exploit his supply line."

sentences.zh: 及其到前，遣奇兵先邀天渡，柴壁左右嚴設伏兵，備其表裏，興欲進不得，住又乏糧。

translations.literal: Before he arrives, send a surprise force first to block Tiandu; set ambushes strictly on both sides of Chaibi to guard inner and outer approaches—if Xing wishes to advance he cannot, if he halts he lacks grain.
translations.idiomatic: "Before he arrives, send a surprise force to cut him off at Tiandu first. Set ambushes firmly on both flanks of Chaibi to cover inner and outer approaches—if Xing tries to advance he cannot, and if he halts he will run short of grain."

sentences.zh: 夫高者為敵所棲，深者為敵所囚，兵法所忌。

translations.literal: The high are roosts for the enemy; the deep are prisons for the enemy—what military treatises forbid.
translations.idiomatic: "High ground becomes a perch for the enemy; deep ground a prison—exactly what the military treatises forbid."

sentences.zh: 而興居之，可不戰而取。

translations.literal: Yet Xing occupies such ground—he can be taken without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet Xing has chosen such ground—he can be taken without a battle."

sentences.zh: 」帝從其計，興果敗歸。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his plan; Xing was indeed defeated and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice; Xing was indeed beaten and fled home.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，問左右：「舊臣中誰為先帝所親信？

translations.literal: When Mingyuan acceded he asked his attendants, "Among the old ministers whom did the late emperor trust most?"
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne he asked his attendants, "Among the old ministers, whom did the late emperor trust most?"

sentences.zh: 」新息公王洛兒曰：「有李先者，為先帝所知。

translations.literal: Duke of Xinxin Wang Luo'er said, "There is Li Xian, whom the late emperor knew well."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Xinxin, Wang Luo'er, said, "There is Li Xian—the late emperor knew him well."

sentences.zh: 」俄而召先，讀韓子《連珠論》二十二篇，《太公兵法》十一事。

translations.literal: Soon Xian was summoned and read twenty-two chapters of Han Fei's Linked Pearls Discourse and eleven items of Taigong's Art of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xian was summoned in and read twenty-two chapters of Han Fei's Linked Pearls Discourse and eleven passages from Taigong's Art of War.

sentences.zh: 詔有司曰：「先所知者，皆軍國大事，自今常宿於內。

translations.literal: An edict to the relevant offices said, "What Xian knows concerns great matters of army and state; from now on let him always lodge within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the relevant offices ran, "What Xian knows touches the great affairs of army and state; henceforth let him lodge always within the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 」賜先絹彩及御馬一匹，拜安東將軍、壽春侯，賜隸戶二十二。

translations.literal: Xian was granted silk brocade and an imperial horse, made General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Shouchun, and given twenty-two dependent households.
translations.idiomatic: He was given silk brocade and an imperial horse, appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Shouchun, and granted twenty-two dependent households.

sentences.zh: 卒於內都大官，年九十五。

translations.literal: He died as Grand Director of the Inner Court at age ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Grand Director of the Inner Court, aged ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 詔賜金縷命服一襲，贈定州刺史、中山公，諡曰文懿。

translations.literal: An edict granted him one suit of gold-threaded life-robes; he was posthumously made Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Zhongshan, with the posthumous name Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he received one suit of gold-threaded life-robes; posthumously he was made Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Zhongshan, with the posthumous name Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子國襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Guo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 國子鳳，中書博士。

translations.literal: Guo's son Feng was an Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's son Feng was an Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鳳子預，字元凱。

translations.literal: Feng's son Yu, styled Yuankai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's son Yu, styled Yuankai.

sentences.zh: 太和初，曆秘書令、齊郡王友、征西大將軍長史，帶馮翊太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he successively served as Director of the Secretariat, Friend to the Prince of Qi Commandery, and Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West, concurrently Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era he served in succession as Director of the Secretariat, Friend to the Prince of Qi Commandery, and Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West, with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 府解，罷郡，遂居長安。

translations.literal: When the staff was dissolved he left the commandery post and settled in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the princely staff was disbanded he relinquished the commandery post and made his home in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 羨古人飧玉法，乃採訪藍田，躬往攻掘，得若環璧雜器形者，大小百餘。

translations.literal: Admiring the ancient method of eating jade, he went to gather it at Lantian, digging in person, and obtained more than a hundred pieces shaped like rings, disks, and miscellaneous vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Enamored of the ancient practice of eating jade, he went to Lantian to gather it, digging with his own hands, and brought back more than a hundred pieces shaped like rings, disks, and other vessels.

sentences.zh: 頗有粗黑者，亦篋盛以還。

translations.literal: Some were rather coarse and black; he boxed them and brought them back all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Some were rather coarse and blackish; he packed them in a box and carried them home anyway.

sentences.zh: 至而觀之，皆光潤可玩。

translations.literal: When he looked at them at home, all were lustrous and pleasing.
translations.idiomatic: When he examined them at home, every piece was lustrous and delightful to handle.

sentences.zh: 預乃椎七十枚為屑食之，余多惠人。

translations.literal: Yu then pounded seventy pieces into powder and ate them, giving most of the rest away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then pulverized seventy pieces and swallowed the powder, giving away most of the rest.

sentences.zh: 後預及聞者更求玉於故處，皆無所見。

translations.literal: Later Yu and others who heard of it searched again at the old spot and found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yu and others who heard the story searched again at the old site but found nothing more.

sentences.zh: 馮翊公源懷弟得其玉，琢為器佩，皆鮮明可寶。

translations.literal: The younger brother of Duke of Fufeng Yuan Huai obtained the jade, carved it into vessels and ornaments—all bright and precious.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother of Duke of Fufeng Yuan Huai acquired the jade and carved it into vessels and personal ornaments, all of them bright enough to be treasured.

sentences.zh: 預服經年，雲有效驗。

translations.literal: Yu took it for more than a year and said it had effect.
translations.idiomatic: Yu consumed it for more than a year and maintained that it worked.

sentences.zh: 而世事寢食，皆不禁節，又加好酒損志。

translations.literal: But worldly affairs gradually encroached on his meals—he observed no restraint—and heavy drinking further harmed his will.
translations.idiomatic: But everyday cares gradually crowded out his meals—he kept no discipline at table—and heavy drinking further dulled his spirit.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，謂妻子曰：「吾酒色不絕，自致於死，非藥過也。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave he told his wife, "I never gave up wine and women and brought myself to death—it is not the medicine's fault.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened he told his wife, "I never gave up wine and women and have brought myself to this end—it is not the jade's fault.

sentences.zh: 然吾屍體必當有異，勿速殯，令後人知飧服之妙。

translations.literal: Yet my corpse will surely show something strange; do not bury me hastily, so that later men may know the marvel of eating jade."
translations.idiomatic: Still, my corpse is sure to show something out of the ordinary; do not bury me in haste, so that men of later times may see the wonder of eating jade."

sentences.zh: 」時七月中旬，長安毒熱，預停屍四宿，而體色不變。

translations.literal: It was mid-seventh month; Chang'an was fiercely hot, yet Yu's body lay four nights and its color did not change.
translations.idiomatic: It was the height of the seventh month; Chang'an sweltered, yet Yu's body lay out four nights without its color changing.

sentences.zh: 其妻常氏，以玉珠二枚琀之，口閉。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Chang placed two jade beads in his mouth as burial pebbles; his mouth closed.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Chang placed two jade beads in his mouth as funerary pebbles; his lips closed.

sentences.zh: 常謂曰：「君自雲飧玉有神驗，何不受琀？

translations.literal: Chang said to him, "You yourself said eating jade had divine proof—why not accept the pebbles?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chang said to him, "You yourself claimed that eating jade worked miracles—why not take the pebbles?"

sentences.zh: 」言訖，齒啟納珠。

translations.literal: When she finished speaking the teeth opened and admitted the beads.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had she spoken than his teeth parted and the beads went in.

sentences.zh: 因噓其口，都無穢氣。

translations.literal: She breathed on his mouth; there was no foul odor at all.
translations.idiomatic: She breathed close to his mouth; there was not the slightest foul smell.

sentences.zh: 舉斂於棺，堅直不傾委。

translations.literal: When they placed him in the coffin he lay straight and did not slump.
translations.idiomatic: When they laid him in the coffin his body remained upright and did not collapse.

sentences.zh: 死時有遺玉屑數升，囊盛納諸棺中。

translations.literal: At death he left several sheng of jade powder in a bag, put into the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he left several sheng of jade powder in a bag, which was placed in the coffin with him.

sentences.zh: 先少子皎。

translations.literal: Xian's younger son Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's younger son Jiao.

sentences.zh: 天興中，密問先曰：「子孫永為魏臣，將復事他姓邪？

translations.literal: In Tianxing, Daowu secretly asked Xian, "Will our descendants forever serve Wei as ministers, or will they serve another surname?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxing era Daowu asked Xian in private, "Will our descendants always remain ministers of Wei, or will they serve another house?"

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「國家政化長遠，不可紀極。

translations.literal: Xian said, "The state's government and transformation extend far—they cannot be reckoned to an end."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The state's governance and transforming influence stretch far into the future—they cannot be traced to an end."

sentences.zh: 」皎為寇謙之弟子，遂服氣絕粒數十年，隱於恆山。

translations.literal: Jiao became a disciple of Kou Qianzhi and then for decades consumed qi and abstained from grain, living in seclusion on Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao became a disciple of Kou Qianzhi and for decades thereafter fed on qi and abstained from grain, living in seclusion on Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 年九十餘，顏如少童。

translations.literal: Past ninety, his face was like a youth's.
translations.idiomatic: Past ninety, his face was like a youth's.

sentences.zh: 一旦，沐浴冠帶，家人異之，俄而坐卒。

translations.literal: One day he bathed, donned cap and belt; his family thought it strange, and soon he sat and died.
translations.idiomatic: One day he bathed, put on cap and sash; his household found it odd, and presently he sat upright and died.

sentences.zh: 道士咸稱其得屍解仙道。

translations.literal: Daoists all called it attaining corpse dissolution and the immortal way.
translations.idiomatic: Daoists everywhere pronounced that he had achieved corpse dissolution and entered the immortal path.

sentences.zh: 皎孫義徽。

translations.literal: Jiao's grandson Yihui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's grandson Yihui.

sentences.zh: 太和中，以儒學博通，有才華，補清河王懌府記室。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, for broad mastery of Confucian learning and literary talent he was made Recorder to Prince Qinghe Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe period, recognized for broad learning in the Confucian classics and for literary gifts, he was made Recorder to Prince Qinghe Yi.

sentences.zh: 箋書表疏，文不加點，清典贍速，當世稱之。

translations.literal: In memorials, letters, and memorials of state his prose needed no revision—clear, canonical, ample, and swift; his age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In official memorials, letters, and submissions his writing needed no polish—lucid, canonical, ample, and swift—and men of his day acclaimed him.

sentences.zh: 又為懌撰《輿地圖》及《顯忠錄》。

translations.literal: He also compiled for Yi the Territorial Map and the Record of Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: For Yi he also drew up the Territorial Map and the Record of Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 性好《老莊》，甚嗤釋教。

translations.literal: By nature he loved Laozi and Zhuangzi and greatly scorned Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament he delighted in Laozi and Zhuangzi and held Buddhism in contempt.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，屬有沙門惠憐以咒水飲人，雲能愈疾，百姓奔湊，日以千數。

translations.literal: When Empress Ling ruled, a monk Huilian charmed water for people to drink, claiming it cured illness; the common folk flocked to him by the thousands daily.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Ling's regency a monk named Huilian gave people water he had "charmed," claiming it cured disease; commoners rushed to him by the thousands each day.

sentences.zh: 義徽白懌，稱其妖妄。

translations.literal: Yihui reported to Yi that this was sorcery and delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yihui reported to Yi that the affair was fraud and delusion.

sentences.zh: 因令義徽草奏以諫，太后納其言。

translations.literal: Yi had Yihui draft a memorial of remonstrance; the empress dowager accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had Yihui compose a remonstrance for the throne; the empress dowager took his advice.

sentences.zh: 元叉惡懌，徙義徽都水使者。

translations.literal: Yuan Cha hated Yi and transferred Yihui to Commissioner of the Metropolitan Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha, who hated Yi, had Yihui transferred to Commissioner of the Metropolitan Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 俄而懌被害，因棄官隱於大房山。

translations.literal: Soon Yi was killed; Yihui therefore abandoned office and lived in seclusion on Mount Dafang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yi was killed; Yihui thereupon resigned his post and went into hiding on Mount Dafang.

sentences.zh: 少子蘭，以純孝著聞，不受辟召。

translations.literal: The younger son Lan was famed for pure filial piety and would not accept summons to office.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Lan won renown for unstinting filial devotion and would not answer summons to office.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，旌表門閭。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang an edict honored his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang an edict honored his gate and lane.

sentences.zh: 正光中，文宣王亶嗣位，思義徽雅正惇篤，薦其孫景儒，位至奉車都尉。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang Prince Wensuan Dan succeeded; remembering Yihui's elegant integrity and steadfast loyalty, he recommended his grandson Jingru, who reached Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era, when Prince Wensuan Dan succeeded, he recalled Yihui's refined integrity and firm loyalty and recommended his grandson Jingru, who rose to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 自皇始至齊受禪，百五十歲。

translations.literal: From Huangshi until Qi received the abdication—one hundred fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huangshi era until Qi received the abdication was a span of one hundred fifty years.

sentences.zh: 先之所言，有明征焉。

translations.literal: What Xian said had clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: What Xian said had clear proof.

sentences.zh: 景儒子昭徽，博涉稽古，脫略不羈，時人稱其為播郎。

translations.literal: Jingru's son Zhaohui ranged widely through antiquity, free and unbound; people of the time called him Gentleman Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Jingru's son Zhaohui ranged widely through antiquity, careless of convention; contemporaries called him "Gentleman Bo."

sentences.zh: 因以字行于燕、趙焉。

translations.literal: He was known by his style in Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was known by his style in Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 善談論，有宏辯，屬文任氣，不拘常則。

translations.literal: Skilled in discourse, with grand eloquence; in writing he followed his own spirit and did not keep to ordinary rules.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in debate and possessed sweeping eloquence; in composition he followed his own bent and ignored ordinary rules.

sentences.zh: 志好隱逸，慕葛洪之為人。

translations.literal: His ambition favored reclusion; he admired Ge Hong's way of life.
translations.idiomatic: He aspired to the life of a recluse and took Ge Hong as his model.

sentences.zh: 尋師訪道，不遠千里。

translations.literal: Seeking teachers and the Way he traveled a thousand li without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: In pursuit of teachers and the Way he would travel a thousand li without flinching.

sentences.zh: 遇高尚則傾蓋如舊，見庸識雖王公蔑如。

translations.literal: Meeting the lofty he inclined his carriage-roof as to an old friend; meeting mediocrity he looked down even on kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the truly lofty he would tilt his carriage awning as to an old acquaintance; toward the mediocre he would look away even from kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 初為道士，中年應詔舉，為高唐尉。

translations.literal: At first he was a Daoist priest; in mid-life he answered the imperial summons and became Wei of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Daoist priest; in middle age he answered the imperial call and was appointed magistrate of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 大業中，將妻子隱于嵩山，號黃冠子。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he took wife and children into seclusion on Mount Song, styling himself Master Yellow Cap.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he withdrew with wife and children to Mount Song, taking the sobriquet Master Yellow Cap.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，為學者所稱。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls, praised by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in ten scrolls, admired by scholars.

sentences.zh: 賈彝，字彥倫，本武威姑臧人也。

translations.literal: Jia Yi, styled Yanlun, was originally of Guzang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi, styled Yanlun, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 六世祖敷，魏幽州刺史、廣川都亭侯，子孫因家焉。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Fu was Wei's Governor of You Province and Marquis of Guangchuan at Douting; the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation forebear Fu had been Governor of You Province for Wei and Marquis of Guangchuan at Douting; the family made its home there.

sentences.zh: 父為苻堅钜鹿太守，坐訕謗系獄。

translations.literal: His father was Fu Jian's Administrator of Julu and was imprisoned for slander.
translations.idiomatic: His father served Fu Jian as Administrator of Julu and was imprisoned for speaking ill of the throne.

sentences.zh: 彝年十歲，詣長安訟父獲申。

translations.literal: Yi at age ten went to Chang'an to plead his father's case and won release.
translations.idiomatic: At ten Yi went to Chang'an to plead his father's case and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 遠近歎之，僉曰：「此子英英，賈誼之後，莫之與京。

translations.literal: Near and far marveled, all saying, "This boy is splendid—a descendant of Jia Yi, none to match in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: People near and far marveled, saying with one voice, "This boy shines like a star—a true descendant of Jia Yi, with none in the capital to equal him."

sentences.zh: 」弱冠，為慕容垂遼西王農記室參軍。

translations.literal: At weak cap he was Agricultural Recorder to Murong Chui's Prince of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he became Agricultural Recorder on the staff of Murong Chui's Prince of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 道武先聞其名，常遣使者求彝于垂，垂彌增器敬。

translations.literal: Daowu had long heard his name and often sent envoys to request Yi from Chui; Chui only increased his respect.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu had long known his reputation and often sent messengers to ask Chui for Yi; Chui only treated him with greater regard.

sentences.zh: 垂遣其太子寶來寇，大敗於參合，執彝及其從兄代郡太守潤等。

translations.literal: Chui sent his heir Bao to raid; at Canhe they were utterly defeated—Yi and his cousin Run, Administrator of Dai Commandery, were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chui sent his heir Bao on a raid; at Canhe they suffered utter defeat, and Yi together with his cousin Run, Administrator of Dai Commandery, were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 道武即位，拜尚書左丞，參預國政。

translations.literal: When Daowu acceded he was made Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and took part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu took the throne he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and took part in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 天賜末，彝請詣溫陽療疾，為叛胡所掠，送于姚興。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianci, Yi asked to go to Wenyang to treat illness and was seized by rebel Hu and delivered to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianci era Yi asked leave to seek treatment at Wenyang, was seized by rebel Hu bands, and sent on to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 積數年遁歸，又為赫連屈丐所執，拜秘書監，卒。

translations.literal: After several years he escaped home, was again seized by Helian Qubing, made Director of the Secretariat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he slipped away and returned home, only to be seized again by Helian Qubing, who made him Director of the Secretariat before he died.

sentences.zh: 太武平赫連昌，子秀迎其屍柩，葬于代南。

translations.literal: When Taiwu pacified Helian Chang, his son Xiu met the coffin and buried him south of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu pacified Helian Chang, his son Xiu went to meet the coffin and buried him south of Dai.

sentences.zh: 秀位中庶子，賜爵陽都男，本州大中正。

translations.literal: Xiu was Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Baron of Yangdu, and Grand Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu served as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, was enfeoffed Baron of Yangdu, and held the post of Grand Rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 獻文即位，進爵陽都子。

translations.literal: When Xianwen acceded he was advanced to Baron of Yangdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianwen acceded, Xiu's title was raised to Baron of Yangdu.

sentences.zh: 時丞相乙渾妻庶姓，而求公主之號，屢言於秀，秀默然。

translations.literal: At the time Chancellor Yi Hun's wife was of common birth yet sought the title of princess; she spoke of it repeatedly to Xiu, who remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chancellor Yi Hun's wife, though of humble birth, repeatedly pressed Xiu for the title of princess; Xiu would not answer.

sentences.zh: 後因公事，就第見渾。

translations.literal: Later on public business he visited Hun at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a matter of official business, he called at Hun's private residence.

sentences.zh: 渾夫妻同坐，厲色曰：「爾管攝職事，無所不從。

translations.literal: Hun and his wife sat together and said harshly, "You oversee duties—nothing should be refused.
translations.idiomatic: Hun and his wife received him together and spoke harshly: "You administer affairs of state—there should be nothing you refuse us.

sentences.zh: 我請公主，不應，何意？

translations.literal: I ask for princess and you do not agree—what do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: I ask for the rank of princess and you withhold your consent—what is your meaning?"

sentences.zh: 」秀慷慨大言對曰：「公主之稱，王姬之號，尊寵之極，非庶族所宜。

translations.literal: Xiu answered boldly, "The title princess, the designation king's daughter—the utmost of honor—is not fitting for a common clan."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu replied with spirit: "The title of princess, the designation of a king's daughter—the summit of favor—is not for a clan of common birth."

sentences.zh: 秀甯就死于今朝，不取笑於後日。

translations.literal: Xiu would rather die this morning than be mocked by posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu would rather die today than be a laughingstock tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」渾左右莫不失色，為之震懼，秀神色自若。

translations.literal: Hun's attendants all changed color and trembled with fear; Xiu's expression was calm as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's men blanched and shook; Xiu's face never changed.

sentences.zh: 渾夫妻默然含忿。

translations.literal: Hun and his wife fell silent, nursing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Hun and his wife said nothing, swallowing their rage.

sentences.zh: 他日，乃書太醫給事楊惠富臂，作「老奴官慳」字，令以示秀。

translations.literal: Another day he wrote on the arm of Chief Medical Attendant Yang Huifu the characters "old slave official stingy," and had him show it to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he had "old-slave-official-stingy" written on Chief Medical Attendant Yang Huifu's arm and shown to Xiu.

sentences.zh: 渾每欲伺隙陷之。

translations.literal: Hun always sought an opening to trap him.
translations.idiomatic: Hun kept watching for a chance to ruin him.

sentences.zh: 會渾伏誅，遂免難。

translations.literal: When Hun was executed in secret, Xiu thus escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Hun was put to death in secret, Xiu escaped.

sentences.zh: 時秀與中書令勃海高允俱以儒舊重于時。

translations.literal: At the time Xiu and Chief Counselor Gao Yun of Bohai, both esteemed as Confucian elders, were heavy in reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and Bohai's Chief Counselor Gao Yun were both famed Confucian elders of the day.

sentences.zh: 皆選擬方嶽，以詢訪被留，各聽長子出為郡。

translations.literal: Both were selected for regional posts, but because of inquiries and consultations were kept at court; each was allowed to send his eldest son out as prefect of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Both were slated for provincial office but kept at court for consultation; each was allowed to send his eldest son out as commandery prefect.

sentences.zh: 秀固讓不受，許之。

translations.literal: Xiu firmly declined and would not accept; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu firmly declined; the court allowed it.

sentences.zh: 自始及終，曆奉五帝。

translations.literal: From beginning to end he served five emperors.
translations.idiomatic: From first to last he served five emperors.

sentences.zh: 雖不至大官，常當機要。
