translations.literal: Though he never reached the highest offices, he was constantly at the pivot of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He never held the highest rank but was always at the heart of affairs.

sentences.zh: 廉清儉約，不營資產。

translations.literal: Upright, pure, and frugal, he did not amass property.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, pure, and spare—he built no fortune.

sentences.zh: 年七十三，遇疾，詔給醫藥，賜几杖。

translations.literal: At age seventy-three he fell ill; an edict provided physicians and medicine and granted folding stool and staff.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-three he fell ill; the throne sent doctors and medicine and granted staff and folding stool.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷舉動及大事不決，每遣尚書、高平公李敷就第訪決。

translations.literal: When the court's actions and great matters were unresolved, they often sent Vice Director Li Fu of Pingyang, Marquis of Gaoping, to his residence for decisions.
translations.idiomatic: When court action or a great matter stalled, Vice Director Li Fu, Marquis of Gaoping, was often sent to his house for a ruling.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冀州刺史、武邑公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Governor of Jizhou, Duke of Wuyi, posthumous name Jian (Simple).
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Governor of Jizhou, Duke of Wuyi, posthumous name Simple.

sentences.zh: 子俊，字異鄰。

translations.literal: His son Jun, styled Yilin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun, styled Yilin.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，位荊州刺史，依例降爵為伯。

translations.literal: Inherited the title, post of Governor of Jingzhou, reduced to marquis per regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title, served as Governor of Jingzhou, and was reduced to marquis by rule.

sentences.zh: 先是，上洛置荊州，後改為洛州，在重山，人不知學，俊表置學官。

translations.literal: Earlier Shangluo had been set as Jingzhou, later changed to Luozhou; among heavy mountains people did not know learning — Jun memorialized to establish school officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shangluo had once been Jingzhou, later Luozhou; in the deep mountains learning was unknown—Jun petitioned to set up school officers.

sentences.zh: 在州五載，清靖寡事，為吏人所安。

translations.literal: Five years in the province, pure and quiet with few affairs, the officials and people were at ease under him.
translations.idiomatic: Five years in office, pure and quiet, little business—the clerks and people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At death posthumously Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 子叔休襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shuxiu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuxiu inherited.

sentences.zh: 潤曾孫禎，字叔願，學涉經史，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Run's great-grandson Zhen, styled Shuyuan, steeped in classics and histories, famed for filial piety in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Run's great-grandson Zhen, styled Shuyuan, steeped in the classics and histories, famed for mourning his parents.

sentences.zh: 太和中，以中書博士副中書侍郎高聰使江左。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, as Doctor of the Secretariat accompanying Vice Director of the Secretariat Gao Cong to Jiangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he went as Secretariat doctor with Vice Director Gao Cong to the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 還，以母老患，輒在家定省，坐免官。

translations.literal: On return, because his mother was old and ill he promptly stayed home to attend her and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: On return his mother was old and ill; he stayed home to nurse her and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒諮議參軍、通直散騎常侍，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later Secretariat Consulting Staff Officer, Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded, with supernumerary title Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Secretariat consulting officer, Regular Attendant Direct and Unimpeded, with supernumerary rank Champion General.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈齊州刺史。

translations.literal: At death posthumously Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 禎兄子景俊，亦以學識知名，為京兆王愉府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Zhen's brother's son Jingjun was also famed for learning, as Outside Military Staff Officer to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's nephew Jingjun was also known for scholarship, outside military staff officer to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.

sentences.zh: 愉起逆于冀州，將授其官；

translations.literal: Yu raised rebellion in Jizhou and was about to appoint him;
translations.idiomatic: Yu rebelled in Jizhou and was about to give him a post;

sentences.zh: 不受，死之。

translations.literal: he would not accept and died for it.
translations.idiomatic: he refused and died for it.

sentences.zh: 贈河東太守，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously Governor of Hedong, posthumous name Zhen (Upright).
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Governor of Hedong, posthumous name Upright.

sentences.zh: 景俊弟景輿，清峻鯁正，為州主簿，遂棲遲不仕。

translations.literal: Jingjun's younger brother Jingyu, pure stern and upright, was chief clerk of a province and then lingered without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun's younger brother Jingyu, stern and upright, was a provincial chief clerk and then would not serve.

sentences.zh: 後葛榮陷冀州，稱疾不拜。

translations.literal: Later when Ge Rong took Jizhou he claimed illness and would not bow.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong seized Jizhou he pleaded illness and would not bow.

sentences.zh: 景輿每捫膝而言曰：「吾不負汝。

translations.literal: Jingyu would stroke his knee and say: "I have not failed you."
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu would pat his knee and say, "I have not failed you."

sentences.zh: 」以不拜榮也。

translations.literal: — for not bowing to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: — for refusing to bow to Rong.

sentences.zh: 竇瑾，字道瑜，頓丘衛國人，自雲漢司空融之後也。

translations.literal: Dou Jin, styled Daoyu, native of Weiguo in Dunqiu, descendant of Han Minister of Works Dou Rong of Yunhan.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin, styled Daoyu, of Weiguo in Dunqiu, descended from Han Minister of Works Dou Rong.

sentences.zh: 高祖成，頓丘太守，因家焉。

translations.literal: Gao ancestor Cheng, Administrator of Dunqiu, made it his home.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Cheng, Administrator of Dunqiu, settled the family there.

sentences.zh: 瑾少以文學知名，自中書博士為中書侍郎，賜爵繁陽子。

translations.literal: Jin from youth was famed for letters; from Doctor of the Secretariat to Vice Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed Viscount of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was famed young for letters; from Secretariat doctor to vice director, enfeoffed Viscount of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 參軍國謀，屢有功，進爵衛國侯，轉四部尚書。

translations.literal: Participated in state counsels with repeated merit, advanced to Marquis of Weiguo, transferred to Director of Four Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in state planning with repeated merit, rose to Marquis of Weiguo, then Director of Four Departments.

sentences.zh: 初定三秦，人猶去就，拜長安鎮將、毗陵公。

translations.literal: When the Three Qins were first pacified and people still wavered, appointed Regional Commander of Chang'an, Duke of Piling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Qins were first settled and allegiance still shifted, he was made Regional Commander of Chang'an, Duke of Piling.

sentences.zh: 在鎮八年，甚著威惠。

translations.literal: Eight years in the command, very distinguished in authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years in command—his authority and kindness were renowned.

sentences.zh: 徵為殿中都官尚書。

translations.literal: Summoned as Director of Palace Attendants and of the Capital Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Director of Palace Attendants and Capital Ministries.

sentences.zh: 太武親待之，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu personally favored him and rewarded him lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu favored him personally and rewarded him richly.

sentences.zh: 從征蓋吳，吳平，留瑾鎮長安。

translations.literal: On campaign against Gai Wu; when Wu was pacified, Jin was left to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Gai Wu; when Wu fell, Jin was left to hold Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 還京復為殿中、都官，典左右執法。

translations.literal: Back in the capital again as Director within the palace and of capital ministries, in charge of law enforcement at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he again directed palace and capital ministries and held law at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 太武歎曰：「國之良輔，毗陵公之謂矣。

translations.literal: Taiwu sighed: "The state's good assistant — that means the Duke of Piling."
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu sighed: "The state's true pillar is the Duke of Piling."

sentences.zh: 」出為冀州刺史，清約沖素，著稱當時。

translations.literal: Out as Governor of Jizhou, pure and abstemious, famed at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as Governor of Jizhou, pure and spare—famed in his day.

sentences.zh: 還為內都大官。

translations.literal: Returned as Grand Director of Palace Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Grand Director of Palace Officials.

sentences.zh: 興光初，瑾女婿郁林公司馬彌陀以選尚臨涇公主，瑾教彌陀辭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingguang, Jin's son-in-law Moduo, marshal of Prince of Yulin, was selected to marry Princess of Linjing; Jin taught Moduo to decline.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingguang 1 Jin's son-in-law Moduo, marshal to Prince of Yulin, was chosen for Princess of Linjing; Jin urged Moduo to refuse.

sentences.zh: 托有誹謗咒詛之言，與彌陀同誅，唯少子遵逃匿得免。

translations.literal: On pretext of slander and curse words, he was executed together with Moduo; only the youngest son Zun escaped by hiding.
translations.idiomatic: On charges of slander and cursing he was executed with Moduo; only the youngest son Zun hid and lived.

sentences.zh: 遵善楷篆，北京諸碑及台殿樓觀宮門題署多遵書。

translations.literal: Zun excelled in regular and seal script; northern capital steles and tower-pavilion palace gate inscriptions were mostly Zun's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Zun excelled in regular and seal script; most northern-capital steles and palace gate inscriptions are his.

sentences.zh: 位濮陽太守，多所受納。

translations.literal: Post of Administrator of Puyang, much accepting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Puyang he took many bribes.

sentences.zh: 其子僧演奸通人婦，為部人賈邈告，坐免。

translations.literal: His son Sengyan fornicated with another man's wife; reported by local man Jia Miao, dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengyan lay with another man's wife; Jia Miao of the district reported him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後以善書拜庫部令，卒官。

translations.literal: Later because of fine calligraphy made Director of Storehouses, died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for fine calligraphy, he was made Director of Storehouses and died in office.

sentences.zh: 李䐶，字元盛，小名真奴，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Xin, styled Yuansheng, childhood name Zhennu, native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin, styled Yuansheng, childhood name Zhennu, of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖產，產子績，二世知名于慕容氏。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Chan, Chan's son Ji — both generations famed under the Murong.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Chan and Chan's son Ji—two generations famed under the Murong.

sentences.zh: 父崇，馮跋吏部尚書、石城太守。

translations.literal: Father Chong, Minister of Civil Service and Administrator of Shicheng under Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong was Minister of Civil Service and Administrator of Shicheng under Feng Ba.

sentences.zh: 車駕至和龍，崇率十餘郡歸降，太武甚禮之，呼曰李公。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Helong, Chong led more than ten commanderies to submit; Taiwu greatly honored him, calling him Lord Li.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Helong, Chong led more than ten commanderies to submit; Taiwu honored him greatly and called him Lord Li.

sentences.zh: 為北幽州刺史、固安侯。

translations.literal: Governor of Northern Youzhou, Marquis of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Northern Youzhou, Marquis of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰襄侯。

translations.literal: At death posthumous title Marquis Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: At death his posthumous title was Marquis Xiang.

sentences.zh: 䐶母賤，為諸兄所輕。

translations.literal: Xin's mother was low-born and was slighted by his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's mother was of humble birth and his elder brothers looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「此子之生，相者言貴，吾每觀，或未可知。

translations.literal: Chong said: "At this child's birth diviners said he would be noble; each time I look, perhaps it cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "At his birth the diviners said he would be noble; each time I look I still cannot tell."

sentences.zh: 」遂使入都為中書學生。

translations.literal: So he sent him to the capital as student of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: So he sent him to the capital as a Secretariat student.

sentences.zh: 太武幸中書學，見而異之，指謂從者曰：「此小兒終效用於朕之子孫。

translations.literal: Taiwu visited the Secretariat school, saw him and thought him unusual, pointed and told followers: "This boy will in the end be useful to my descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu visited the Secretariat school, saw him, thought him unusual, and said to his attendants, "This boy will one day serve my house."

sentences.zh: 」因識眄之。

translations.literal: So he took special notice of him.
translations.idiomatic: So he marked him for special notice.

sentences.zh: 帝舅陽平王杜超有女，將許貴戚，帝曰：「李䐶後必官達，益人門戶，可以妻之。

translations.literal: The emperor's uncle Duke of Yangping Du Chao had a daughter to be given to a noble house; the emperor said: "Li Xin will surely reach high office and benefit another's gate — she can be wife to him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's uncle Duke of Yangping Du Chao had a daughter for a noble match; the emperor said, "Li Xin will surely rise and enrich another house—give her to him."

sentences.zh: 」遂勸成婚。

translations.literal: So he urged the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: So he pressed the marriage.

sentences.zh: 南人李哲常言䐶必當貴達。

translations.literal: The southerner Li Zhe often said Xin would surely reach noble eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The southerner Li Zhe often said Xin would surely reach high rank.

sentences.zh: 杜超之死也，帝親哭三日。

translations.literal: When Du Chao died the emperor himself mourned three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chao died the emperor mourned him in person for three days.

sentences.zh: 䐶以超女婿，得在喪位出入。

translations.literal: Xin as Chao's son-in-law was able to come and go in mourning quarters.
translations.idiomatic: As Chao's son-in-law Xin could enter and leave the mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 帝指謂左右曰：「觀此人舉動，豈不異於眾也？

translations.literal: The emperor pointed and said to attendants: "Watch this man's bearing — is it not unlike the crowd?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pointed him out and said, "Look at this man's bearing—is it not unlike the crowd?"

sentences.zh: 必為朕家幹事臣。

translations.literal: He will surely be a capable minister for my house.
translations.idiomatic: He will surely be a pillar of my house.

sentences.zh: 」䐶聰敏機辯，強記明察。

translations.literal: Xin was quick, clever, argumentative, with strong memory and sharp perception.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was quick, clever, sharp-tongued, with a strong memory and keen eye.

sentences.zh: 初，李靈為文成博士，詔崔浩選中書學生器業優者為助教。

translations.literal: Initially Li Ling was Wencheng's erudite; edict for Cui Hao to select the best students of the Secretariat school as assistant teachers.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Ling was Wencheng's erudite; an edict had Cui Hao pick the best Secretariat students as assistant teachers.

sentences.zh: 浩舉其弟子箱子與盧度世、李敷三人應之。

translations.literal: Hao nominated his disciple Son Xiang, Lu Duanshi, and Li Fu — three to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Hao named his pupil Son Xiang, Lu Duanshi, and Li Fu.

sentences.zh: 給事高讜子祐、尚書段霸兒侄等以為浩阿党其親戚，言于景穆。

translations.literal: Gaoyan's son You and Duan Ba's nephew and others said Hao showed favoritism to kin, told Jingmu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyan's son You and Duan Ba's nephew and others said Hao favored kin and told Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 以浩為不平，聞之于太武。

translations.literal: As Hao was unfair, it reached Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: The charge of unfairness reached Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 太武意在䐶，曰：「云何不取幽州刺史李崇老翁兒？

translations.literal: Taiwu had Xin in mind and said: "Why not take old man Li Chong's son of Youzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu had Xin in mind and said, "Why not take old Li Chong's boy from Youzhou?"

sentences.zh: 」浩對曰：「前亦言䐶合選，但以其先行在外，故不取之。

translations.literal: Hao replied: "Earlier I also said Xin fit selection, but because he was first traveling outside, was not taken."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "I said Xin fit before, but he was away and was not taken."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「可待䐶還，箱子等罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can wait for Xin to return and dismiss Xiang and the others."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wait until Xin returns and dismiss Xiang and the rest."

sentences.zh: 」遂除中書助教、博士，入授文成經。

translations.literal: So made assistant teacher and erudite of Secretariat, entered to teach Wencheng the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was made assistant teacher and Secretariat erudite and taught Wencheng the classics.

sentences.zh: 文成即位，䐶以舊恩親寵，遷儀曹尚書，領中秘書，賜爵扶風公。

translations.literal: Wencheng acceded; Xin for old favor was intimate and favored, promoted Master of Rites, concurrently head of Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffed Duke of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencheng took the throne Xin, for old favor, was intimate and favored—Master of Rites, head of the Imperial Secretariat, Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 贈其母孫氏為容城君。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Sun was enfeoffed Lady of Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Sun was made Lady of Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 帝顧群臣曰：「朕始學之歲，情未能專；

translations.literal: The emperor told the ministers: "In the year I first studied I could not concentrate;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers, "When I first studied I could not fix my mind;

sentences.zh: 既總萬機，溫習靡暇。

translations.literal: having assumed all affairs there was hardly leisure to warm old lessons.
translations.idiomatic: once I held all affairs I had no leisure to review old lessons.

sentences.zh: 是故儒道實有闕焉。

translations.literal: Thus in truth the Confucian way had gaps — not only my fault
translations.idiomatic: So the Confucian way truly had gaps—not mine alone

sentences.zh: 豈惟予咎，抑亦師傅之不勤。

translations.literal: but also the teachers' lack of diligence.
translations.idiomatic: but also my teachers' slackness.

sentences.zh: 所以爵賞仍隆，蓋不遺舊也。

translations.literal: Therefore rank and reward remain lofty — I do not forget the old."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore rank and reward stay high—I do not forget the old days."

sentences.zh: 」䐶免冠拜謝。

translations.literal: Xin doffed cap and bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Xin removed his cap and bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 出為相州刺史。

translations.literal: Out as Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: His government was pure and simple; the common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was pure and simple; the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 䐶上疏求於州郡各立學官，使士望之流，衣冠之胄，就而受業。

translations.literal: Xin memorialized asking that each province and commandery establish school officials so men of local standing and gentry scions could come to study.
translations.idiomatic: Xin petitioned that every province and commandery set up schools so local worthies and gentry sons could study.

sentences.zh: 其經藝通明者，上王府。

translations.literal: Those penetrating in the classics would go up to the princely mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Those who mastered the classics would enter the princes' households.

sentences.zh: 書奏，獻文從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; Xianwen approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up; Emperor Xianwen approved.

sentences.zh: 以䐶政為諸州之最，加賜衣服。

translations.literal: Because Xin's governance was the best among the provinces, extra robes were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's governance was judged best among the provinces and extra robes were granted.

sentences.zh: 自是遂有驕矜自得之志，受納人財物，商胡珍寶。

translations.literal: From then on he had a proud, self-satisfied air, accepting people's goods and merchants' treasures.
translations.idiomatic: From then on pride took him; he took people's goods and merchants' treasures.

sentences.zh: 兵人告言。

translations.literal: Soldiers reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers reported him.

sentences.zh: 尚書李敷與䐶少長相好，每左右之。

translations.literal: Vice Director Li Fu and Xin had been close from youth; Fu always shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Li Fu and Xin had been close since youth; Fu always covered for him.

sentences.zh: 或有勸以奏聞，敷不許。

translations.literal: Some urged reporting to the throne; Fu would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged reporting to the throne; Fu forbade it.

sentences.zh: 獻文聞䐶罪狀，檻車征䐶，拷劾抵罪。

translations.literal: Xianwen heard of Xin's crimes, sent a caged cart to summon Xin, and tortured him to establish guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen heard of Xin's crimes, summoned him in a cage-cart, and tortured him to conviction.

sentences.zh: 敷兄弟將見疏斥，有司諷以中旨嫌敷兄弟之意，令䐶告列敷等隱罪，可得自全。

translations.literal: The Fu brothers were about to be cast off; the authorities hinted at the inner will's dislike of the Fu brothers and had Xin report and list Fu's hidden crimes so he could save himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu brothers were to be cast aside; the authorities hinted at the throne's dislike and told Xin to denounce Fu's hidden crimes to save himself.

sentences.zh: 䐶深所不欲，且弗之知也，乃謂其女婿裴攸曰：「吾與李敷，族世雖遠，情如一家。

translations.literal: Xin did not want this and also did not know the matter; he then said to his son-in-law Pei You: "Li Fu and I, though our clans are far apart, are close as one family.
translations.idiomatic: Xin did not want it and claimed ignorance; he told his son-in-law Pei You, "Li Fu and I are distant kin but close as kin.

sentences.zh: 在事既有此勸，昨來引簪自刺，以帶自絞，而不能致絕。

translations.literal: In office there was this urging; yesterday I drew a hairpin and stabbed myself, took a belt and strangled myself, yet could not die.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed me in office; yesterday I stabbed myself with a hairpin and strangled with a belt and still could not die.

sentences.zh: 且亦不知其事。

translations.literal: And I also do not know the affair."
translations.idiomatic: And I do not even know the affair."

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「何為為他死？

translations.literal: You said: "Why die for another?"
translations.idiomatic: You said, "Why die for someone else?"

sentences.zh: 敷兄弟事釁可知。

translations.literal: The Fu brothers' guilt is plain.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu brothers' guilt is obvious.

sentences.zh: 有馮闌者，先為敷殺，其家切恨之。

translations.literal: There is one Feng Lan whom Fu had killed earlier; that family hates him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lan was killed by Fu before; his family hates Fu bitterly.

sentences.zh: 但呼闌弟問之，足可知委。

translations.literal: Just call Lan's younger brother and ask — enough to know the whole.
translations.idiomatic: Call Lan's younger brother and ask—that is enough to know everything.

sentences.zh: 」䐶從其言。

translations.literal: Xin followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xin did as he said.

sentences.zh: 又趙郡範標具列敷兄弟事狀，有司以聞，敷坐得罪。

translations.literal: Also Fan Biao of Zhao commandery fully listed the Fu brothers' conduct; the authorities reported upward, and Fu was convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Biao of Zhao also laid out the Fu brothers' deeds; the authorities reported up and Fu was convicted.

sentences.zh: 詔列䐶貪冒應死，以糾李敷兄弟，故免。

translations.literal: An edict listed Xin's greed as deserving death, but because he had exposed the Fu brothers he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said Xin's greed deserved death, but because he had exposed the Fu brothers he was spared.

sentences.zh: 百鞭髡刑，配為廝役。

translations.literal: One hundred lashes, tonsure, and assignment as menial.
translations.idiomatic: He received a hundred lashes, was shaved, and made a menial.

sentences.zh: 䐶之廢也，平壽侯張讜見䐶，與語，奇之。

translations.literal: When Xin was disgraced, Marquis of Pingshou Zhang Dan saw Xin and spoke with him, finding him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin fell, Marquis of Pingshou Zhang Dan met him and found him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「此佳士也，終不久屈。

translations.literal: He told others: "This is a fine man; he will not long remain bent."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This is a fine man; he will not stay bent long."

sentences.zh: 」未幾而復為太倉尚書，攝南部事。

translations.literal: Before long he was again Grand Director of the Granary, acting southern-section affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again Grand Director of the Granary, acting for the southern section.

sentences.zh: 用范標陳策計，令千里之外，戶別轉運，詣倉輸之。

translations.literal: Using Fan Biao's submitted plan, he ordered that beyond a thousand li each household separately transport grain to the granary.
translations.idiomatic: He used Fan Biao's plan: beyond a thousand li each household had to transport grain to the granary.

sentences.zh: 使所在委滯，停延歲月。

translations.literal: This made localities pile up grain, stalled for months.
translations.idiomatic: Local stores piled up and stalled for months.

sentences.zh: 百姓競以貨賂，各求在前，於是遠近大為困弊。

translations.literal: The people competed with bribes to get ahead in line; near and far were greatly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: People bribed to go first; near and far were ruined.

sentences.zh: 道路群議曰：「畜聚斂之人，未若盜臣。

translations.literal: The roads resounded with talk: "A hoarding minister is worse than a thieving minister."
translations.idiomatic: On the roads people said, "A hoarding minister is worse than a thief minister."

sentences.zh: 」䐶弟左軍將軍璞謂䐶曰：「範標善能降人以色，假人以辭，未聞德義之言，但有勢利之說。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Left Army General Pu said to Xin: "Fan Biao is good at winning men with a pleasant face and lending them fine words; one never hears talk of virtue and duty, only of power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's brother Pu, Left Army General, said, "Fan Biao wins men with a pleasant face and fine words; you never hear virtue, only profit.

sentences.zh: 聽其言也甘，察其行也賊，所謂諂諛讒慝，貪冒奸佞。

translations.literal: His words taste sweet; watch his deeds and they are thievish — the so-called flatterer, slanderer, greedy traitor.
translations.idiomatic: His words are sweet; his deeds are theft—flatterer, slanderer, greedy traitor.

sentences.zh: 不早絕之，後悔無及。

translations.literal: If you do not cut him off early, regret will not reach you."
translations.idiomatic: Cut him off now or regret it later."

sentences.zh: 」䐶不從，彌信之，腹心事皆以告標。

translations.literal: Xin would not listen, trusted him all the more, and told Biao everything in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xin would not listen; he trusted Biao more and told him every secret.

sentences.zh: 䐶既寵于獻文，參決軍國大議，兼典選舉，權傾內外，百寮莫不曲節以事之。

translations.literal: Xin was favored by Xianwen, took part in deciding great military and state counsels, also held selection of officials — power tilted inside and outside; the hundred offices all bent the knee to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by Xianwen, Xin joined in army and state counsels and held selection; power leaned inside and out; every office bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 標以無功起家拜盧奴令。

translations.literal: Biao for no merit was enfeoffed and made magistrate of Lu'nu.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, without merit, was made magistrate of Lu'nu.

sentences.zh: 獻文崩，䐶遷司空，進爵范陽公，出為侍中、鎮南大將軍、開府儀同三司、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xianwen died, Xin was moved to Minister of Works, advanced to Duke of Fanyang, out as Palace Attendant, Regional Commander of the South, General Who Opens Offices with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianwen died Xin became Minister of Works, Duke of Fanyang, Palace Attendant, Regional Commander of the South, General Opening Offices with Three Excellencies' rank, Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 范標知文明太后之忿䐶，又知內外疾之，太和元年，希旨告䐶外叛。

translations.literal: Fan Biao knew Empress Dowager Wenming's anger at Xin and knew inside and outside resented him; in Taihe year 1 he reported to her will that Xin was plotting outside rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Biao knew Empress Dowager Wenming hated Xin and that court and country resented him; in Taihe 1 he reported Xin was plotting rebellion outside.

sentences.zh: 文明太后征䐶至京師，言其叛狀。

translations.literal: The empress dowager summoned Xin to the capital and stated his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned Xin to the capital and charged rebellion.

sentences.zh: 䐶曰：「無之。

translations.literal: Xin said: "There is none."
translations.idiomatic: Xin said, "There is none."

sentences.zh: 」引標證䐶。

translations.literal: Biao was brought to testify against Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was called to testify against Xin.

sentences.zh: 䐶言：「爾妄雲知我，吾又何言！

translations.literal: Xin said: "You falsely claim to know me — what more can I say!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin said, "You lie that you know me—what can I say!"

sentences.zh: 雖然，爾不顧餘之厚德，而忍為此，不仁甚矣。

translations.literal: "Yet you disregard the deep kindness I showed you and could bear this — inhuman in the extreme."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you forget my deep kindness and do this—inhuman in the extreme."

sentences.zh: 」標曰：「公德于標，何若李敷之德於公？

translations.literal: Biao said: "Your grace to Biao — how does it compare with Li Fu's grace to you?"
translations.idiomatic: Biao said, "Your grace to me—how does it compare with Fu's grace to you?"

sentences.zh: 公昔忍於敷，標今敢不忍公乎？

translations.literal: "You once could bear to harm Fu; how dare Biao not bear to harm you now?"
translations.idiomatic: You once harmed Fu; how dare I not harm you now?"

sentences.zh: 」䐶慨然曰：「吾不用璞言，自貽伊戚，萬悔于心，何嗟及矣！

translations.literal: Xin sighed: "I did not heed Pu's words and brought this grief on myself — ten thousand regrets in the heart; too late to sigh!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin sighed, "I ignored Pu and brought this on myself—regret beyond words, too late to sigh!"

sentences.zh: 」遂見誅。

translations.literal: He was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed.

sentences.zh: 璞字季直，性惇厚，多識人物。

translations.literal: Pu, styled Jizhi, nature thick and honest, knew many men.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, styled Jizhi, was thick and honest and knew many men.

sentences.zh: 賜爵宜陽侯，太常卿。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang, Grand Minister of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang, Grand Minister of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 韓延之，字顯宗，南陽堵陽人，魏司徒暨之後也。

translations.literal: Han Yanzhi, styled Xianzong, native of Duyang in Nanyang, descendant of Wei Minister of Works Han Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, styled Xianzong, of Duyang in Nanyang, descended from Wei Minister of Works Han Ji.

sentences.zh: 仕晉，位建威將軍、荊州從事，轉平西府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Served Jin, post of General Who Establishes Might, staff officer of Jingzhou, transferred to chief clerk of the Pacify-the-West headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served Jin as General Who Establishes Might, Jingzhou staff officer, then chief clerk of the Pacify-the-West headquarters.

sentences.zh: 晉將劉裕伐司馬休之，未至江陵，密與延之書招之。

translations.literal: When Jin general Liu Yu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, before reaching Jiangling he secretly wrote Yanzhi a letter to win him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, before reaching Jiangling he secretly wrote to win Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 延之報書，辭甚激厲，曰：「劉裕足下：海內之人，誰不見足下此心，而復欲欺誑國士！

translations.literal: Yanzhi replied; the words were very fierce: "Liu Yu beneath your feet: who in the realm does not see your heart, yet you would again deceive the state's gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's reply was fierce: "Liu Yu, every man under heaven sees your heart—yet you would deceive the state's gentlemen again!"

sentences.zh: 」其不屈如此。

translations.literal: His unbending was thus.
translations.idiomatic: He was that unbending.

sentences.zh: 事見《南史宋本紀》。

translations.literal: The affair is in the Basic Annals of Song in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is in Song's Basic Annals in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 延之以裕父名翹，字顯宗，於是己字顯宗，名子為翹，蓋示不臣劉氏也。

translations.literal: Because Yu's father's name was Qiao, styled Xianzong, Yanzhi therefore styled himself Xianzong and named his son Qiao — showing he would not serve the Liu house.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's father's name was Qiao, styled Xianzong; Yanzhi styled himself Xianzong and named his son Qiao—refusing to serve the Liu.

sentences.zh: 後奔姚興。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fled to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 泰常二年，與司馬文思等俱入魏。

translations.literal: In Taichang year 2 he entered Wei with Sima Wensi and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang 2 he entered Wei with Sima Wensi and others.

sentences.zh: 明元以延之為武牢鎮將，賜爵魯陽侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan made Yanzhi Regional Commander of Wulao, enfeoffed Marquis of Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan made him Regional Commander of Wulao, Marquis of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 初，延之曾來往柏穀塢，省魯宗之墓，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Earlier Yanzhi had come and gone at Bai'gu Walled Town, visited the tomb of Lu Zongzhi, and had a mind to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had visited Lu Zongzhi's tomb at Bai'gu Walled Town and wished to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 因謂之孫云：「河洛三代所都，朝廷必有居此者。

translations.literal: He therefore told Zongzhi's grandson: "The Luo and Yi rivers were capitals for three dynasties; the court will surely dwell here.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zongzhi's grandson, "Luo and Yi were capitals for three dynasties; the court will surely live here.

sentences.zh: 我死，不勞向北代葬也，即可就此。

translations.literal: When I die, do not trouble to bury me in Northern Dai; you may bury me right here."
translations.idiomatic: When I die do not bury me in Northern Dai—bury me here."

sentences.zh: 」子從其言，遂葬宗之墓次。

translations.literal: The son followed his words and buried him beside Zongzhi's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: His son obeyed and buried him by Zongzhi's tomb.

sentences.zh: 延之後五十餘年而孝文徙都，其孫數家即居於祖墓之北柏穀塢。

translations.literal: More than fifty years later Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital; several of Yanzhi's households lived north of the ancestral tomb at Bai'gu Walled Town.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty years later Xiaowen moved the capital; Yanzhi's kin lived north of the tomb at Bai'gu.

sentences.zh: 袁式，字季祖，陳郡陽夏人，漢司徒滂之後。

translations.literal: Yuan Shi, styled Jizu, native of Yangxia in Chen commandery, descendant of Han Minister of Works Yuan Pang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shi, styled Jizu, of Yangxia in Chen, descended from Han Minister of Works Yuan Pang.

sentences.zh: 父深，晉侍中。

translations.literal: Father Shen, Jin Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen was Jin Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 式在南，曆武陵王遵諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Shi in the south held the post of Consulting Staff Officer to Prince of Wuling Wang Zun.
translations.idiomatic: In the south Shi was consulting staff officer to Prince of Wuling Wang Zun.

sentences.zh: 及劉裕執權，式歸姚興。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu seized power, Shi went to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu seized power Shi went to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 及姚泓滅，歸魏，為上客，賜爵陽夏子。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed he came to Wei as a honored guest, enfeoffed Viscount of Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong fell he came to Wei as honored guest, Viscount of Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 與司徒崔浩一面，便盡國士之交。

translations.literal: With Minister of Works Cui Hao one meeting made them sworn friends as men of the state.
translations.idiomatic: One meeting with Cui Hao made them sworn friends as men of the state.

sentences.zh: 時朝儀典章悉出於浩，浩以式博於故事，每所草創，恆顧訪之。

translations.literal: At the time court ritual and statutes all came from Hao; Hao because Shi was broad in old precedents, whenever he drafted something always consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual then came from Hao; Hao, because Shi knew old precedent, always consulted him when drafting.

sentences.zh: 性長者，雖羈旅飄泊，而清貧守度，不失士節。

translations.literal: By nature a man of long years; though drifting in exile he kept pure poverty and measure, not losing a gentleman's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of long years; though exiled he stayed poor and measured, never losing a gentleman's line.

sentences.zh: 時人甚敬重之，皆呼曰袁諮議。

translations.literal: Men of the time greatly respected him; all called him Consultant Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His time respected him; all called him Consultant Yuan.

sentences.zh: 至延和二年，衛大將軍、樂安王範為雍州刺史，詔式與中書侍郎高允俱為從事中郎。

translations.literal: In Yanhe year 2, Defender-General Prince of Le'an Fan was Governor of Yongzhou; edict had Shi and Vice Director of Secretariat Gao Yun both as consulting staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanhe 2 Prince of Le'an Fan, Defender-General, was Governor of Yong; Shi and Secretariat Vice Director Gao Yun were made his consulting officers.

sentences.zh: 辭而獲免。

translations.literal: He declined and was excused.
translations.idiomatic: He declined and was excused.

sentences.zh: 式沈靖樂道，周覽書傳，至於詁訓《倉》、《雅》，偏所留懷。

translations.literal: Shi was serene and loved the Way, broadly read records and transmissions, especially fond of glossing the Cangjie and Erya.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was serene, loved the Way, read widely, especially glossing Cangjie and Erya.

sentences.zh: 作《字釋》未就。

translations.literal: He composed "Explanation of Characters" but did not finish.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Explanation of Characters" but did not finish.

sentences.zh: 乙太安二年卒，贈豫州刺史，諡肅侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yitai'an he died, posthumously Governor of Yuzhou, posthumous name Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: In Yitai'an 2 he died, posthumously Governor of Yuzhou, posthumous name Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 子濟襲父爵，位魏郡太守，政有清稱。

translations.literal: Son Ji inherited the father's title, post of Administrator of Wei commandery, government with a pure reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Son Ji inherited, was Administrator of Wei commandery, famed for pure rule.

sentences.zh: 加甯遠將軍。

translations.literal: Added title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He was given supernumerary rank General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 及宋王劉昶開府，召為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Song Liu Chang opened his headquarters, Ji was summoned as consulting staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Song Liu Chang opened headquarters Ji was summoned as consulting officer.

sentences.zh: 毛修之，字敬文，滎陽陽武人也。

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, styled Jingwen, native of Yangwu in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi, styled Jingwen, of Yangwu in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 世仕晉。

translations.literal: For generations the house served Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His house served Jin for generations.

sentences.zh: 劉裕之平關中，留子義真鎮長安，以修之為司馬。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu pacified Guanzhong he left his son Yizhen to garrison Chang'an, making Xiuzhi marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu pacified Guanzhong he left son Yizhen at Chang'an with Xiuzhi as marshal.

sentences.zh: 及義真敗，修之沒統萬。

translations.literal: When Yizhen was defeated Xiuzhi was taken at Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhen fell Xiuzhi was taken at Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 太武平赫連昌，獲之。

translations.literal: When Taiwu pacified Helian Chang he obtained him.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu pacified Helian Chang and took him.

sentences.zh: 使領吳兵，以功拜吳兵將軍。

translations.literal: He was made to lead Wu troops; for merit enfeoffed General of Wu Troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was set to lead Wu troops and enfeoffed General of Wu Troops for merit.

sentences.zh: 修之能為南人飲食，手自煎調，多所適意。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi could make southern food and personally season it, often to satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi could cook southern food and season it himself to please.

sentences.zh: 太武親待之，累遷尚書，賜爵南郡公，常在太官主進禦膳。

translations.literal: Taiwu personally favored him, repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Masters of Writing, enfeoffed Duke of Nan commandery, constantly in the Imperial Kitchen directing imperial meals.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu favored him, raised him to Vice Director, Duke of Nan, always in the Imperial Kitchen directing meals.

sentences.zh: 從討和龍，時諸軍攻城，行宮人少，宋故將硃修之為雲中將軍，欲率吳兵為逆。

translations.literal: On campaign against Helong, when the armies besieged the city the traveling palace had few men; Song's old general Zhu Xiuzhi was General of Yunzhong and wished to lead Wu troops in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Helong the camp had few men; Song's Zhu Xiuzhi, General of Yunzhong, wished to lead Wu troops in revolt.

sentences.zh: 因入和龍，冀浮海南歸。

translations.literal: He entered Helong hoping to float south by sea and return.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Helong hoping to sail south by sea.

sentences.zh: 以告修之，不聽，乃止。

translations.literal: He told Xiuzhi; Xiuzhi would not listen and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xiuzhi; Xiuzhi refused and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 是日無修之，大變幾作。

translations.literal: That day without Xiuzhi a great upheaval nearly happened.
translations.idiomatic: That day without Xiuzhi a great disaster nearly came.

sentences.zh: 硃修之遂奔馮弘。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi then fled to Feng Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi fled to Feng Hong.

sentences.zh: 修之又以軍功，遷特進、撫軍大將軍，位次崔浩下。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi again for military merit was promoted Special Advancement, General Who Pacifies the Army, rank below Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi rose again for merit to Special Advancement, General Who Pacifies the Army, below Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩以其中國舊門，雖不博洽，猶涉獵書傳，與共論說之。

translations.literal: Hao because he was an old house of China, though not broadly versed still dipped into books and records, and debated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, because he was an old Chinese house, though not broad still read books and debated with him.

sentences.zh: 次及陳壽《三國志》，云「有古良史風，其所著述，文義典正，班史以來無及壽者」。

translations.literal: Next they reached Chen Shou's "Records of the Three Kingdoms"; he said "it has the air of an ancient good historian; what he wrote is canonical in meaning — since Ban Gu none match Shou."
translations.idiomatic: They came to Chen Shou's "Records of the Three Kingdoms"; Hao said it had the air of a good ancient historian, canonical since Ban Gu.

sentences.zh: 修之曰：「昔在蜀中，聞長老言，壽曾為諸葛亮門下書佐，得撻百下，故其論武侯云：應變非其所長。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi said: "In Shu I once heard elders say Shou had been a clerk under Zhuge Liang and was flogged a hundred strokes, so in judging the Martial Lord he wrote: adapting to change was not his strength."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi said, "In Shu elders said Shou had been Zhuge Liang's clerk, was flogged a hundred times, so he wrote the Martial Lord was weak at adaptation."

sentences.zh: 」浩乃與論曰：「承祚之評亮，乃有故義過美之譽，非挾恨之言。

translations.literal: Hao then argued: "Chen Shou's judgment of Liang was praise beyond measure from old obligation, not words of resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Hao argued, "Shou's judgment of Liang was old obligation praising too much, not resentment."

sentences.zh: 夫亮之相備，英雄奮發之時，君臣相得，魚水為喻。

translations.literal: Liang's serving Bei was the time when hero and lord met; ruler and minister matched, fish and water as metaphor.
translations.idiomatic: Liang serving Bei was hero and lord meeting, ruler and minister like fish and water.

sentences.zh: 而不能與曹氏爭天下，委棄荊州，退入巴蜀，守窮崎嶇之地，僭號邊夷之間，此策之下者。

translations.literal: Yet he could not contend with Cao for the realm, abandoned Jingzhou, retreated into Ba-Shu, held poor rugged ground, styled himself emperor among border barbarians — this is the lowest stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not fight Cao for the realm, abandoned Jingzhou, retreated to Ba-Shu, held poor hills, styled himself emperor among barbarians—the lowest stratagem.

sentences.zh: 可以趙佗為偶，而以管、蕭之亞匹，不亦過乎！

translations.literal: He may be paired with Zhao Tuo, yet to rank with Guan Zhong and Xiao He — is that not excessive!
translations.idiomatic: He may match Zhao Tuo; to rank with Guan Zhong and Xiao He—is that not too much!

sentences.zh: 且亮既據蜀，弗量勢力，嚴威切法，控勒蜀人，欲以邊夷之眾，抗衡上國。

translations.literal: Moreover Liang held Shu, did not measure strength, used harsh law to control Shu men, wished with border barbarians' masses to resist the central state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Liang held Shu, misread strength, ruled Shu with harsh law, wished border tribes to resist the center.

sentences.zh: 出兵隴右，再攻祁山，一攻陳倉，疏遲失會，摧衄而反。

translations.literal: He sent troops out Longyou, twice attacked Qishan, once attacked Chencang, slow and missing the moment, broken and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He marched from Longyou, twice attacked Qishan, once Chencang, slow and late, broken and back.

sentences.zh: 後入秦川，更求野戰。

translations.literal: Later he entered Qin River valley and again sought field battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered Qinchuan and again sought battle in the open.

sentences.zh: 魏人知其意，以不戰屈之。

translations.literal: The Wei men knew his intent and wore him down without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Wei knew his mind and wore him down without fighting.

sentences.zh: 智窮勢盡，發病而死。

translations.literal: Wits exhausted, power spent, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wits gone, power spent, he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，豈合古之善將，見可知難乎？

translations.literal: By this speaking, how does he fit an ancient good general who sees difficulty and knows when to stop?
translations.idiomatic: By that measure, how is he an ancient good general who sees difficulty and stops?

sentences.zh: 」修之謂浩言為然。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi said Hao's words were right.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi said Hao was right.

sentences.zh: 後卒於外都大官，諡恭公。

translations.literal: Later he died as Grand Director of the Outer Capital Kitchen, posthumous name Duke Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died as Grand Director of the Outer Capital Kitchen, posthumous Duke Gong.

sentences.zh: 修之在南有四子，唯子法仁入魏。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi in the south had four sons; only son Faren entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the south Xiuzhi had four sons; only Faren entered Wei.

sentences.zh: 文成初，為金部尚書，襲爵，轉殿中尚書。

translations.literal: At the start of Wencheng he was Director of the Gold Bureau, inherited the title, transferred to Director Within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At Wencheng's start he was Director of the Gold Bureau, inherited the title, then Director Within the Hall.

sentences.zh: 法仁言聲壯大，至於軍旅田狩，唱呼處分，振於山谷。

translations.literal: Faren's voice was strong and large; in army camp and hunt his shouts directing ranks shook the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Faren's voice was huge; on campaign and hunt his commands shook the valleys.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征東大將軍、南郡王，諡曰威。

translations.literal: At death posthumously General Who Pacifies the East, Prince of Nan commandery, posthumous name Wei (Martial).
translations.idiomatic: At death posthumously General Who Pacifies the East, Prince of Nan, posthumous name Martial.

sentences.zh: 硃修之者，仕宋為司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi had served Song as consulting staff officer to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi had served Song as consulting staff officer to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 守滑台，為安頡所禽。

translations.literal: He held Huatai and was captured by An Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He held Huatai and was taken by An Ji.

sentences.zh: 太武善其固守，以宗室女妻之，以為雲中鎮將。

translations.literal: Taiwu praised his firm defense, gave him an imperial-clan woman in marriage, made him Regional Commander of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu praised his defense, married him an imperial-clan woman, made him Regional Commander of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 後奔馮弘。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Feng Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fled to Feng Hong.

sentences.zh: 弘送之江南。

translations.literal: Hong sent him to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent him to the south.

sentences.zh: 頡之克滑，宋陳留太守嚴稜戍倉垣。

translations.literal: When Ji took Huatai, Song's Administrator of Chenliu Yan Ling garrisoned Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji took Huatai, Song's Chenliu Administrator Yan Ling held Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 及山陽公奚斤軍至潁川，稜率文武五百人詣斤降。

translations.literal: When Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin's army reached Yingchuan, Ling led five hundred civil and military men to Jin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin reached Yingchuan, Ling led five hundred officials and soldiers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 明元嘉其誠款，賜爵郃陽侯，假荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Mingyuan praised his sincere submission, enfeoffed Marquis of Heyang, acting Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan praised his sincerity, enfeoffed Marquis of Heyang, acting Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 隨駕南討，還為上客。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial campaign south, returned as honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the southern campaign and returned as honored guest.

sentences.zh: 及太武踐阼，以歸化之功，除中山太守，有清廉稱。

translations.literal: When Taiwu ascended, for merit in submission he was made Administrator of Zhongshan, famed for pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu took the throne, for submitting he was made Administrator of Zhongshan, famed for purity.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子幼玉襲。

translations.literal: Son Youyu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Youyu inherited.

sentences.zh: 稜舊書有傳，今附之云。

translations.literal: Ling once had a separate biography; now it is appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Ling once had his own biography; it is appended here.

sentences.zh: 修之在宋顯達，事並具《南史》。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was eminent in Song; the affairs are fully in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was eminent in Song; the full account is in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 唐和，字幼起，晉西宜安人也。

translations.literal: Tang He, styled Youqi, native of Xiyi'an in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He, styled Youqi, of Xiyi'an in Jin.

sentences.zh: 父繇，以涼土喪亂，推涼武昭王霸於河右。

translations.literal: Father Yao, because Liang lands were in turmoil, installed Liang Wuzhao Wang Ba in the lands west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao, when Liang was in chaos, set up Wuzhao Wang Ba west of the river.

sentences.zh: 及涼亡，和與兄契攜其甥武昭王孫寶，避難伊吾。

translations.literal: When Liang fell, He and elder brother Qi took their nephew, Wuzhao Wang's grandson Bao, and fled to Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell He and brother Qi took nephew Bao, Wuzhao's grandson, and fled to Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 招集人眾二千餘家，臣於蠕蠕。

translations.literal: He gathered more than two thousand households and submitted to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered more than two thousand households and submitted to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕以契為伊吾王。

translations.literal: The Rouran made Qi King of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran made Qi King of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 經二十年，和與契遣使降魏，為蠕蠕所逼，遂擁部至高昌。

translations.literal: After twenty years He and Qi sent envoys to surrender to Wei but were pressed by the Rouran and therefore led their tribes to Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty years they sent envoys to Wei; the Rouran pressed them and they led their people to Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕遣部帥阿若討和，至白力城。

translations.literal: The Rouran sent a tribal chief A Ruo to attack He, reaching Baili City.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran sent chief A Ruo against He to Baili City.

sentences.zh: 和先攻高寧。

translations.literal: He first attacked Gaoning.
translations.idiomatic: He first attacked Gaoning.

sentences.zh: 契與阿若戰沒，和收餘眾，奔前部國。

translations.literal: Qi fought A Ruo and fell; He gathered the remainder and fled to the Former Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Qi fought A Ruo and died; He gathered the rest and fled to the Former Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 時沮渠安周屯橫截城，和攻拔之。

translations.literal: At the time Juqu Anzhou held Hengjie City; He attacked and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Anzhou held Hengjie City; He took it.

sentences.zh: 斬安周兄子樹，又克高甯、白力二城。

translations.literal: He beheaded Anzhou's nephew Shu, also took Gaoning and Baili cities.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Anzhou's nephew Shu and took Gaoning and Baili.

sentences.zh: 遣使表狀。

translations.literal: He sent a memorial reporting.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a memorial reporting.

sentences.zh: 太武嘉之，屢賜之璽書。

translations.literal: Taiwu praised him and repeatedly granted sealed edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu praised him and repeatedly sent sealed edicts.

sentences.zh: 後和與前部王車伊洛破安周。

translations.literal: Later He and the Former Kingdom's king Che Yiluo destroyed Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later He and Former Kingdom king Che Yiluo destroyed Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 太武使周公萬度歸討焉耆，詔和與伊洛率所領赴度歸，喻下柳驢以東六城。

translations.literal: Taiwu sent Duke of Zhou Wan Dugui to campaign against Yanqi; edict had He and Yiluo lead their followers to Dugui and persuade the six cities east of Liulü.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu sent Wan Dugui against Yanqi; He and Yiluo were to join him and win the six cities east of Liulü.

sentences.zh: 因共擊波居羅城，拔之。

translations.literal: Together they attacked Bojuluo City and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Together they attacked Bojuluo City and took it.

sentences.zh: 後同征龜茲，度歸令和鎮焉耆。

translations.literal: Later on joint campaign against Kucha, Dugui ordered He to garrison Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: On joint campaign against Kucha Dugui left He to hold Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 時柳驢戍主乙真伽將叛，和徑入其城，禽斬乙真伽。

translations.literal: At the time the garrison chief of Liulü, Yizhenjia, was about to rebel; He went straight into his city and seized and beheaded Yizhenjia.
translations.idiomatic: Liulü garrison chief Yizhenjia was about to rebel; He entered his city and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 由是西域克平，和有力焉。

translations.literal: By this the Western Regions were pacified; He had strength in it.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions were pacified; He had a hand in it.

sentences.zh: 子欽，字孟真，位陝州刺史。

translations.literal: Son Qin, styled Mengzhen, post of Governor of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Son Qin, styled Mengzhen, was Governor of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 降爵為侯。

translations.literal: Reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His title was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒，子景宣襲爵。

translations.literal: At death son Jingxuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: At death son Jingxuan inherited.

sentences.zh: 卒于東都太守。

translations.literal: Died as Administrator of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Administrator of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 契子玄達，性果毅，有父風。

translations.literal: Qi's son Xuanda, nature resolute and bold, had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's son Xuanda was resolute and bold like his father.

sentences.zh: 與叔父和歸闕，俱為上客，封晉昌公。

translations.literal: With uncle He he came to court and both were honored guests, enfeoffed Duke of Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: With uncle He he came to court; both were honored guests, enfeoffed Duke of Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 獻文時，位華州刺史。

translations.literal: In Xianwen's time post of Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianwen's time he was Governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 太和十六年，降為侯。

translations.literal: In Taihe year 16 reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 16 he was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 子崇，字繼祖，襲爵。

translations.literal: Son Chong, styled Jizu, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chong, styled Jizu, inherited.

sentences.zh: 寇贊，字奉國，上穀人也，因難徙馮翊萬年。

translations.literal: Kou Zan, styled Fengguo, native of Shanggu, because of hardship moved to Wan'nian in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zan, styled Fengguo, of Shanggu, moved to Wan'nian in Fengyi in hardship.

sentences.zh: 父修之，字延期，苻堅東萊太守。

translations.literal: Father Xiuzhi, styled Yanqi, Administrator of Donglai under Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Father Xiuzhi, styled Yanqi, was Donglai Administrator under Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 贊弟謙，有道術，太武敬重之，故追贈修之安西將軍、秦州刺史、馮翊公。

translations.literal: Zan's younger brother Qian had the Way; Taiwu greatly respected him, therefore posthumously made Xiuzhi General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qinzhou, Duke of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Qian had the Way; Taiwu respected him and posthumously made Xiuzhi General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Qin, Duke of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 賜命服，諡曰哀公。

translations.literal: Granted funeral robes, posthumous name Duke Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral robes were granted, posthumous Duke Ai.

sentences.zh: 詔秦、雍二州為立碑墓。

translations.literal: Edict had Qin and Yong provinces erect stele and tomb.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Qin and Yong erect stele and tomb.

sentences.zh: 又贈修之母為馮翊夫人，及宗從追贈太守、縣令、侯、子、男者十六人，其臨職者七郡、五縣。

translations.literal: Also posthumously made Xi's mother Lady of Fengyi, and sixteen clansmen posthumously administrators, magistrates, marquises, viscounts, barons — seven commanderies and five counties in active office.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's mother was made Lady of Fengyi; sixteen kin were posthumously administrators, magistrates, and nobles—seven commanderies, five counties in office.

sentences.zh: 贊少以清潔知名。

translations.literal: Zan from youth was famed for purity.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was famed young for purity.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，姿容嚴嶷，非禮不動。

translations.literal: Eight feet tall, bearing stern and lofty, he did not move outside ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet tall, stern bearing—he would not stir outside ritual.

sentences.zh: 苻堅僕射韋華，州裏高達，雖年時有異，恆以風味相待。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's Vice Director Wei Hua, a lofty man of the province, though years differed always treated him with shared taste.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's Vice Director Wei Hua, a provincial worthy, though older always treated him as an equal in taste.

sentences.zh: 華為馮翊太守，召為功曹。

translations.literal: When Hua was Administrator of Fengyi he summoned Zan as merit officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua was Fengyi Administrator he summoned Zan as merit officer.

sentences.zh: 後除襄邑令。

translations.literal: Later made magistrate of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made magistrate of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 姚泓滅，秦、雍人千餘家推贊為主，歸魏。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed more than a thousand families of Qin and Yong made Zan their leader and came to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong fell more than a thousand Qin and Yong families made Zan leader and came to Wei.

sentences.zh: 拜河南郡太守。

translations.literal: Made Administrator of Henan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 其後秦、雍人來奔河南、滎陽、河內者，戶至萬數，拜贊南雍州刺史、軹縣侯，於洛陽立雍州之郡縣以撫之。

translations.literal: Afterward Qin and Yong men who fled to Henan, Xingyang, and Henei reached ten thousand households; Zan was made Governor of Southern Yong, Marquis of Zhiji, and Yong province commanderies and counties were set up at Luoyang to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Later ten thousand Qin and Yong households fled to Henan, Xingyang, and Henei; Zan was Southern Yong Governor, Marquis of Zhiji, with Yong counties at Luoyang to settle them.

sentences.zh: 由是流人繈負，自遠而至，參倍於前。

translations.literal: Thus refugees came on backs and in slings from afar, more than double before.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees came on backs and in slings from afar, more than double before.

sentences.zh: 進贊爵河南公，加安南將軍，領南蠻校尉，仍刺史。

translations.literal: Zan's rank advanced to Duke of Henan, added General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel of the Southern Man, still governor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Duke of Henan, General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel of the Southern Man, still governor.

sentences.zh: 分洛、豫二州之僑郡以益之。

translations.literal: Luoyang and Yuzhou refugee commanderies were added to his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang and Yuzhou refugee commanderies were added.

sentences.zh: 雖位高爵重，接待不倦。

translations.literal: Though rank and title were heavy he never tired in receiving people.
translations.idiomatic: Though rank was heavy he never tired of receiving people.

sentences.zh: 初，贊之未貴，嘗從相者唐文相。

translations.literal: Earlier before Zan was noble he once had physiognomist Tang Wen read him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was noble Zan had physiognomist Tang Wen read him.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「君額上黑子入幘，位當至方伯，封公。

translations.literal: Wen said: "The black mole on your brow enters the cap — rank will reach regional lord, enfeoffed duke."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "The black mole on your brow enters the cap—you will reach regional lord, be enfeoffed duke."

sentences.zh: 」及其貴也，文以百姓禮拜謁曰：「明公憶疇昔言乎？

translations.literal: When he was noble Wen came in commoner's rites and bowed: "My lord, do you recall what I said before?"
translations.idiomatic: When he was noble Wen bowed as a commoner: "My lord, do you recall my words?"

sentences.zh: 」延文坐曰：「往時卿言杜瓊不得官長，人咸謂不然。

translations.literal: Yanwen sat and said: "In the past you said Du Qiong could not be a chief official; all thought otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwen sat and said, "You once said Du Qiong could not be chief official; all disagreed.

sentences.zh: 及瓊為盩厔令，卿猶言相中不見，而瓊果以暴疾，未拜而終。

translations.literal: When Qiong became magistrate of Zhouzhi you still said the physiognomy did not show it, yet Qiong indeed died suddenly of violent illness before taking office."
translations.idiomatic: When Qiong became Zhouzhi magistrate you said the face did not show it—yet Qiong died suddenly before taking office."

sentences.zh: 昔魏舒見主人兒死，自知己必至公。

translations.literal: In old times Wei Shu saw his master's son die and knew he himself would reach duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu once saw his master's son die and knew he would reach duke.

sentences.zh: 吾恆以卿言瓊之驗，亦復不息此望也。

translations.literal: I always took your judgment of Qiong as proof and never ceased this hope."
translations.idiomatic: I always took your judgment of Qiong as proof and never lost hope."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜文衣服良馬。

translations.literal: He therefore granted Wen robes and a fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: He granted Wen robes and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 贊在州十七年，甚收公私之譽。

translations.literal: Zan seventeen years in the province greatly won public and private praise.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen years in the province he won public and private praise.

sentences.zh: 年老，求致仕。

translations.literal: Old, he asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺令薄葬，斂以時服。

translations.literal: At death he ordered a thin burial in timely dress.
translations.idiomatic: At death he ordered thin burial in timely dress.

sentences.zh: 太武悼惜之，諡曰宣穆。

translations.literal: Taiwu mourned him, posthumous name Duke Xuanmu.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu mourned him, posthumous Duke Xuanmu.

sentences.zh: 子元寶襲爵。

translations.literal: Son Yuanbao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yuanbao inherited.

sentences.zh: 元寶弟臻，字仙勝。

translations.literal: Yuanbao's younger brother Zhen, styled Xiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zhen, styled Xiansheng.

sentences.zh: 年十二，遭父憂，居喪以孝稱。

translations.literal: At twelve he met father's death; in mourning famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he met his father's death; mourning made him famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 輕財好士。

translations.literal: Light with wealth, fond of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He was light with wealth and fond of scholars.

sentences.zh: 獻文末，為中川太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianwen he was Administrator of Zhongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xianwen he was Administrator of Zhongchuan.

sentences.zh: 時馮熙為洛州刺史，政號貪虐，仙勝微能附之，甚得其意。

translations.literal: At the time Feng Xi was Governor of Luozhou, government marked by greed and cruelty; Xiansheng slightly attached to him and greatly won his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi was Luozhou Governor, greedy and cruel; Xiansheng attached to him slightly and won his favor.

sentences.zh: 後為弘農太守。

translations.literal: Later Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Later Administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 坐受納，為御史所彈，遂廢，卒於家。

translations.literal: Convicted of taking bribes, impeached by the censor, dismissed, died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of bribes, impeached by the censor, dismissed, died at home.

sentences.zh: 子祖訓，順陽太守。

translations.literal: Son Zuxun, Administrator of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zuxun, Administrator of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 祖訓弟祖禮。

translations.literal: Zuxun's younger brother Zuli.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxun's younger brother Zuli.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並孝友敦穆，白首同居。

translations.literal: The brothers were all filial, friendly, and grave; white-haired they dwelt together.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were filial, friendly, and grave; white-haired they lived together.

sentences.zh: 父母亡雖久，猶于平生所處堂宇，備設幃帳几杖，以時節開堂列拜；

translations.literal: Though parents had long died, in the hall where they had lived in life they still set curtains, folding stools, and staffs, and at seasons opened the hall and bowed in rows;
translations.idiomatic: Though parents were long dead, in their old hall they still set curtains, stools, and staffs; at seasons they opened the hall and bowed in rows;

sentences.zh: 垂涕陳薦，若宗廟焉。

translations.literal: weeping they offered sacrifice as at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: weeping they offered sacrifice as at a temple.

sentences.zh: 吉凶之事，必先啟告，遠出行反亦如之。

translations.literal: For auspicious or inauspicious matters they always reported first; returning from a distant journey was the same.
translations.idiomatic: For good or ill they always reported first; returning from travel was the same.

sentences.zh: 祖禮，宣武末為河州刺史。

translations.literal: Zuli at the end of Emperor Xuanwu was Governor of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zuli at the end of Xuanwu was Governor of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 在任數年，遇郤鐵匆反，又為城人詣都列其貪狀十六條。

translations.literal: Several years in office he met Xi Tiejiong's sudden rebellion; also city men went to the capital to list sixteen articles of his greed.
translations.idiomatic: In office he met Xi Tiejiong's rebellion; city men also listed sixteen charges of greed at court.

sentences.zh: 會赦免。

translations.literal: He was spared by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼廷尉卿，又兼尚書。

translations.literal: After long time concurrently Commandant of the Court, also concurrently Vice Director of Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Long after he was concurrently Court Commandant and Vice Director of Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 畏避勢家，承顏候色，不能有所執據。

translations.literal: He feared powerful houses, accommodated their faces and colors, and could not hold to principle.
translations.idiomatic: He feared powerful houses, accommodated their moods, and could not hold principle.

sentences.zh: 後蠻反於三鴨，為都督追討，戰歿。

translations.literal: Later when barbarians rebelled at Sanya he was commander pursuing them and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later barbarians rebelled at Sanya; as commander he pursued them and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈衛大將軍、七兵尚書、雍州刺史、昌平男。

translations.literal: Posthumously Defender-General, Director of Seven Armies, Governor of Yongzhou, Baron of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Defender-General, Director of Seven Armies, Governor of Yong, Baron of Changping.

sentences.zh: 祖禮弟俊。

translations.literal: Zuli's younger brother Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zuli's younger brother Jun.

sentences.zh: 俊字祖俊。

translations.literal: Jun styled Zujun.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was styled Zujun.

sentences.zh: 性寬雅，幼有識量，好學強記。

translations.literal: By nature broad and elegant, from youth had judgment, loved learning and strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: Broad and elegant by nature, from youth he had judgment, loved learning, remembered well.

sentences.zh: 性又廉恕，不以財利為心。

translations.literal: By nature also lenient and forgiving, he did not set his heart on wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He was also lenient and forgiving and did not set his heart on wealth.

sentences.zh: 家人曾賣物與人，而利得絹一匹。

translations.literal: The household once sold goods to someone and wrongly gained one bolt of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The household once sold goods and wrongly gained one bolt of silk.

sentences.zh: 俊於後知之，乃曰：「得財失行，吾所不取。

translations.literal: When Jun learned of it afterward, he said: "To gain wealth and lose conduct—what I will not take."
translations.idiomatic: When Jun learned of it later he said, "Wealth gained, conduct lost—that I will not take."

sentences.zh: 」訪主還之。

translations.literal: He sought out the buyer and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: He found the buyer and returned the silk.

sentences.zh: 以選為孝文帝挽郎，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: By selection he became a mourning attendant for Emperor Xiaowen and was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a mourning attendant for Xiaowen, he was made Court Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 大乘賊起，燕、趙擾亂，俊參護軍事東討，以功授員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Dacheng bandits rose and Yan and Zhao were thrown into disorder, Jun joined the staff on the eastern campaign; for merit he was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Dacheng rebels threw Yan and Zhao into turmoil, Jun served on the eastern staff and was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant for merit.

sentences.zh: 累遷司空府主簿。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Chief Clerk in the Minister of Works office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Chief Clerk in the Minister of Works office.

sentences.zh: 時靈太后臨朝，減食祿官十分之一，造永寧佛寺，令俊典之。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Ling held court, cut salaries of officeholders by a tenth, and built Yongning Buddhist Temple, putting Jun in charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Ling held court she cut official salaries by a tenth and built Yongning Temple, putting Jun in charge.

sentences.zh: 資費巨萬，主吏不能欺隱。

translations.literal: Costs ran to tens of millions, yet the chief clerks could not conceal anything from him.
translations.idiomatic: Costs ran to tens of millions; chief clerks could not hide a thing from him.

sentences.zh: 寺成，又極壯麗。

translations.literal: When the temple was finished, it was also magnificently grand.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple stood complete, it was magnificently grand.

sentences.zh: 靈太后嘉之，除左軍將軍。

translations.literal: Empress Ling praised him and appointed him General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling praised him and made him General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，朝議以國用不足，乃置鹽池都將，秩比上郡。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era the court debated that state revenue was insufficient and therefore established a Salt-Pool Commandant, rank equal to a superior commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang the court, finding revenue short, established a Salt-Pool Commandant equal in rank to a superior commandery.

sentences.zh: 前後居職者多有侵隱，乃以俊為之，仍主簿。

translations.literal: Those who held the post before and after often embezzled; Jun was therefore put in it while still chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier holders had often embezzled; Jun was appointed while still chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 永安初，華州人史底與司徒楊椿訟田。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan, a man of Huazhou named Shi Di sued Minister of Works Yang Chun over fields.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongan, Shi Di of Huazhou sued Minister of Works Yang Chun over land.

sentences.zh: 長史以椿勢貴，皆言椿直，欲以田給椿。

translations.literal: The chief administrator, because Chun was powerful and noble, all said Chun was in the right and wished to give the fields to Chun.
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator, seeing Chun's power, all sided with him and meant to award the land to Chun.

sentences.zh: 俊曰：「史底窮人，楊公橫奪其地，若欲損不足以給有餘，見使雷同，未敢聞命。

translations.literal: Jun said: "Shi Di is a poor man; Lord Yang seized his land by force. If you would harm the insufficient to enrich the ample, and make me echo the crowd, I dare not obey."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Shi Di is a poor man whom Lord Yang robbed. To strip the wanting to feed the full, and make me echo the crowd—I dare not obey."

sentences.zh: 」遂以地還史底。

translations.literal: He therefore returned the land to Shi Di.
translations.idiomatic: The land was returned to Shi Di.

sentences.zh: 孝莊帝后知之，嘉俊守正不撓，拜司馬；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang learned of it afterward and praised Jun for holding firm without bending; he was made Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang learned of it and praised Jun's upright refusal; he was made Marshal.

sentences.zh: 其附椿者咸責焉。

translations.literal: Those who had sided with Chun all blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had sided with Chun blamed Jun.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he went out as Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he went out as Inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 人俗荒獷，多為盜賊。

translations.literal: The people were wild and rough; many became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Custom was wild; banditry was common.

sentences.zh: 俊乃令郡縣為立庠序，勸其耕桑，敦以禮讓。

translations.literal: Jun then ordered the commanderies and counties to establish schools, urged them to plow and raise silkworms, and taught them through ritual and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered schools built, urged farming and sericulture, and taught courtesy and yielding.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，風俗頓革。

translations.literal: Within several years custom was suddenly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Within years custom was transformed.

sentences.zh: 梁遣其將曹琰之鎮魏興，繼日板築。

translations.literal: Liang sent its general Cao Yanzhi to hold Weixing, piling ramparts day after day.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Cao Yanzhi to hold Weixing, raising ramparts daily.

sentences.zh: 琰之屢擾疆場，邊人患之。

translations.literal: Yanzhi repeatedly harassed the border; frontier people were troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi harried the frontier; border folk suffered.

sentences.zh: 俊遣長史杜林道攻克其城，並禽琰之。

translations.literal: Jun sent Chief Administrator Du Lindao to storm the city and capture Yanzhi as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Chief Administrator Du Lindao to take the city and capture Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 琰之即梁大將景宗之季弟也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was the youngest brother of Liang's great general Xiao Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was youngest brother to Liang's great general Xiao Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 於是梁人懼焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the men of Liang were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang were afraid.

sentences.zh: 屬魏室多故，州又僻遠，梁人知無外援，遂大兵頓魏興，志圖攻取。

translations.literal: As Wei affairs were many and the province remote, the Liang knew there was no outside aid and massed troops at Weixing, intent on taking it.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei in turmoil and the province remote, Liang knew no aid would come and massed at Weixing to take it.

sentences.zh: 俊撫厲將士，人思效命。

translations.literal: Jun comforted and roused his officers and men; all thought to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Jun comforted his troops; all wished to die for him.

sentences.zh: 梁人知其得眾心也，弗之敢逼。

translations.literal: The Liang, knowing he had won the hearts of the masses, did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he held the army's hearts, Liang did not dare press him.

sentences.zh: 俊在州清苦，不事產業，其子等並徒步而還。

translations.literal: Jun in the province lived plainly and did not pursue estates; his sons and the rest all walked home on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Jun lived plainly in the province, built no estates; his sons walked home on foot.

sentences.zh: 吏人送俊，留連於道，久之乃得出界。

translations.literal: Officials and people escorted Jun and lingered on the road; only after long time did he cross the border.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people escorted him, lingering on the road long before he left the border.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，東魏授俊洛州刺史，俊因此乃謀歸闕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Eastern Wei appointed Jun Inspector of Luozhou; Jun therefore plotted to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year three Eastern Wei made him Inspector of Luoyang; he plotted to return to court.

sentences.zh: 五年，將家及親屬四百口入關，拜秘書監。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he brought his household and four hundred kin into the Pass and was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he brought family and four hundred kin through the Pass and was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時軍國草創，墳典散逸，俊始選置令史，抄集經籍，四部群書，稍得周備。

translations.literal: At the time the army and state were newly founded and classics scattered; Jun first selected clerks to copy and gather the canon—gradually the four divisions of books became fairly complete.
translations.idiomatic: With the state newly founded and classics scattered, Jun chose clerks to copy books; the four divisions grew fairly complete.

sentences.zh: 加鎮東將軍，封安西縣男。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed Baron of Anxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and Baron of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加散騎常侍，遂稱篤疾，不復朝覲。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then claimed grave illness and no longer attended court.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then pleaded grave illness and stopped attending court.

sentences.zh: 恭帝三年，賜姓若口引氏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Gongdi he was granted the surname Ruokouyin.
translations.idiomatic: In Gongdi year three he was granted the surname Ruokouyin.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, his rank was advanced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaomin took the throne his rank rose to viscount.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he was advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of the same rites as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year one he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Three-Duke rites.

sentences.zh: 俊年齒雖高，而志識未衰。

translations.literal: Though Jun's years were high, his will and understanding had not declined.
translations.idiomatic: Though old, his mind had not declined.

sentences.zh: 教授子孫，必先典禮。

translations.literal: In teaching his sons and grandsons he always began with ritual and propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching sons and grandsons, he always began with ritual.

sentences.zh: 明帝尚儒重德，特欽賞之，數加思賜，思與相見。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming honored Confucian learning and prized virtue and especially admired him, repeatedly bestowing favors and wishing to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Ming honored learning and virtue, admired him, sent gifts, and wished to see him.
