sentences.zh: 俊不得已，乃入朝，帝與同席而坐，顧訪洛陽故事。

translations.literal: Jun could not refuse and entered court; the emperor sat with him on the same mat and asked about old stories of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun entered court; the emperor shared his mat and asked about Luoyang of old.

sentences.zh: 俊身長八尺，須鬢皓然，容止端詳，音韻清朗。

translations.literal: Jun was eight feet tall, beard and whiskers snow-white, bearing dignified and composed, voice clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet tall, beard snow-white, bearing composed, voice clear.

sentences.zh: 帝與之談論，不覺屢為之前膝。

translations.literal: In discussion with him the emperor unconsciously shifted forward on his knees again and again.
translations.idiomatic: In talk with him the emperor, without noticing, drew his knees forward again and again.

sentences.zh: 及俊辭還，帝親執其手，曰：「公年德俱尊，朕所欽尚。

translations.literal: When Jun took leave to return, the emperor personally held his hand and said: "Sir, your years and virtue are both honored—what I admire in you.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun left, the emperor held his hand and said, "Your years and virtue are both honored—that is what I admire.

sentences.zh: 乞言之事，所望於公。

translations.literal: Matters of begging your counsel are what I hope from you.
translations.idiomatic: I look to you for counsel.

sentences.zh: 宜數相見，以慰虛想。

translations.literal: You should often come to see me, to ease my empty longing."
translations.idiomatic: Come often, to ease my longing."

sentences.zh: 」以禦輿令於帝前乘出。

translations.literal: He had the imperial carriage wait for Jun to ride out before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He had the imperial carriage brought for Jun to ride out before him.

sentences.zh: 顧謂左右曰：「如此事，唯積善者可以致之。

translations.literal: Turning to those at his side he said: "Such things only one who has long accumulated goodness can attain.
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants, "Only long-accumulated goodness wins such things.

sentences.zh: 何止見重於今，亦將傳之萬古。

translations.literal: How much more than being honored today—it will be handed down ten thousand ages."
translations.idiomatic: More than honor today—it will live ten thousand ages."

sentences.zh: 」時人咸以為榮。

translations.literal: Men of the time all considered it glory.
translations.idiomatic: All the age called it glory.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十二。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘆惜之，贈本官，加冀定瀛三州諸軍事、冀州刺史，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sighed in regret and posthumously granted his former offices, adding Overseer of Military Affairs for Ji, Ding, and Ying Provinces and Inspector of Ji, posthumous name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sighed, granted his former offices, added Overseer of Ji, Ding, and Ying and Inspector of Ji, posthumous name Yuan.

sentences.zh: 俊篤于仁義，期功之中有孤幼者，衣食豐約，並與之同。

translations.literal: Jun was devoted to humaneness and righteousness; among those within mourning obligation who were orphaned and young, in food and clothing plenty or want he shared alike with them.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to humaneness, he shared food and clothing with orphaned kin within mourning obligation.

sentences.zh: 少為司徒崔光所知，光命其子勵與俊結友。

translations.literal: In youth he was known to Minister of Works Cui Guang; Guang ordered his son Li to befriend Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Cui Guang knew him and ordered his son Li to befriend Jun.

sentences.zh: 俊每造光，常清談移日。

translations.literal: Whenever Jun visited Guang they would talk in pure conversation until the day moved on.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jun visited Guang they talked until the day was gone.

sentences.zh: 小宗伯盧辯以俊業行俱崇，待以師友之禮。

translations.literal: Junior Preceptor of the Clan Lu Bian, because Jun's achievement and conduct were both lofty, treated him with the rites due teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bian, seeing Jun's conduct lofty, treated him as teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 每有閒暇，輒詣俊宴語彌日。

translations.literal: Whenever he had leisure he would go to Jun and feast in talk a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure he feasted and talked with Jun whole days.

sentences.zh: 恆謂人曰：「不見安西君，煩憂不遣。

translations.literal: He would always tell people: "If I do not see Lord Anxi, vexation will not leave me."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Without Lord Anxi, vexation never leaves."

sentences.zh: 」其為通人所敬重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which the learned world held him.
translations.idiomatic: So the learned world esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 子奉，位至儀同大將軍、順陽郡守、洵州刺史、昌國縣公。

translations.literal: His son Feng reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with army credentials, Administrator of Shunyang, Inspector of Xun, and Duke of Changguo.
translations.idiomatic: Son Feng reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with army credentials, Shunyang Administrator, Xun Inspector, Duke of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 奉弟顒，少好學，最知名。

translations.literal: Feng's younger brother Yong was fond of learning and most famed.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Yong loved learning and was most famed.

sentences.zh: 居喪哀毀。

translations.literal: In mourning he was destroyed by grief.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning grief destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 位儀同大將軍，掌朝、布憲、典祀下大夫，小納言，濩澤郡公。

translations.literal: He held Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with army credentials, Lower Grand Masters for Court, Proclamation of Laws, and Sacrificial Rites, Junior Remonstrator, and Duke of Huoze.
translations.idiomatic: He held army credentials as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, lower grand masters for court, law, and sacrifice, Junior Remonstrator, Duke of Huoze.

sentences.zh: 酈範，字世則，范陽涿鹿人也。

translations.literal: Li Fan, styled Shize, was a man of Zhuolu in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, styled Shize, came from Zhuolu in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖紹，慕容寶濮陽太守，以郡迎降，道武授兗州監軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was Administrator of Puyang under Murong Bao; he welcomed the surrender of the commandery and Daowu made him Overseer of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Shao was Puyang Administrator under Murong Bao; he welcomed surrender and Daowu made him Overseer of Yan.

sentences.zh: 父嵩，天水太守。

translations.literal: His father Song was Administrator of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Father Song was Tianshui Administrator.

sentences.zh: 范，太武時，給事東宮。

translations.literal: Fan, in Emperor Taiwu's time, was attendant in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiwu's time Fan served the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太武踐阼，追錄先朝舊勳，賜爵永寧男。

translations.literal: When Taiwu took the throne he recorded old merit of the former court and granted the rank Baron of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu took the throne he recorded prior merit and made Fan Baron of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 以奉禮郎奉遷太武、景穆神主於太廟，進爵為子。

translations.literal: As Director of Ceremonial Offerings he escorted the spirit tablets of Taiwu and Jingmu to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was advanced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: As Director of Ceremonial Offerings he escorted Taiwu and Jingmu to the temple and was advanced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 為征南大將軍慕容白曜司馬。

translations.literal: He was Chief Clerk to Grand General of the South Murong Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: He was Chief Clerk to Grand General of the South Murong Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 及定三齊，範多進策，白曜皆用其謀，遂表為青州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Three Qi were pacified Fan offered many plans; Baiyao used all his stratagems and therefore memorialized him as Inspector of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Qi fell Fan offered many plans; Baiyao used them all and memorialized him Inspector of Qing.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，加冠軍將軍，還為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to marquis, made Champion General, and returned as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced to marquis and Champion General, he returned Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後除平東將軍、青州刺史，假范陽公。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing, with acting title Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Qing, acting Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 范前解州還京也，夜夢陰毛拂踝。

translations.literal: When Fan earlier left his province and returned to the capital, at night he dreamed of dark hair brushing his ankle.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan earlier left the province for the capital he dreamed dark hair brushed his ankle.

sentences.zh: 他日說之。

translations.literal: Another day he spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he told the dream.

sentences.zh: 時齊人有占夢者史武進云：「公豪盛于齊下矣。

translations.literal: At the time a man of Qi skilled in dream-reading, Shi Wujin, said: "My lord, your splendor already lies below Qi."
translations.idiomatic: A Qi dream-reader, Shi Wujin, said, "My lord, your splendor already lies below Qi."

sentences.zh: 」使君臨撫東秦，道光海岱，必當重牧全齊，再祿營丘矣。

translations.literal: "When my lord oversees and comforts Eastern Qin, your light covers the sea and Mount Tai—you will surely again shepherd all Qi and receive a second fief at Yingqiu."
translations.idiomatic: "When you oversee Eastern Qin and your light covers sea and Mount Tai, you will again shepherd all Qi and receive Yingqiu a second time."

sentences.zh: 」範笑答曰：「吾將為卿必驗此夢。

translations.literal: Fan laughed and replied: "I will make this dream come true for you."
translations.idiomatic: Fan laughed, "I will make this dream true for you."

sentences.zh: 」果如言。

translations.literal: It turned out as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It came to pass as he said.

sentences.zh: 時鎮將元伊利表範與外賊交通。

translations.literal: At the time the garrison commander Yuan Yili memorialized that Fan trafficked with outside bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Yuan Yili reported Fan trafficked with outside bandits.

sentences.zh: 孝文詔範曰：「鎮將伊利表卿造船市玉，與外賊交通，規陷卿罪，窺覦州任。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen edicted Fan: "Garrison commander Yili reports that you built ships and bought jade, trafficked with outside bandits, plotted to frame you, and eyed your provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen edicted, "Yili says you built ships and bought jade, trafficked with bandits, framed you, and coveted your province.

sentences.zh: 有司推驗，虛實自顯，有罪者今伏其辜矣。

translations.literal: The offices investigated; truth and falsehood will show themselves—the guilty have now paid their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation will show truth; the guilty have paid.

sentences.zh: 卿其明為算略，勿復懷疑。

translations.literal: You should plan clearly and not doubt again."
translations.idiomatic: Plan clearly and doubt no more."

sentences.zh: 」還朝，卒京師。

translations.literal: He returned to court and died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court and died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 子道元。

translations.literal: His son Daoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Son Daoyuan.

sentences.zh: 道元字善長。

translations.literal: Daoyuan, styled Shanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan, styled Shanchang.

sentences.zh: 初襲爵永甯侯，例降為伯。

translations.literal: At first he inherited the rank Marquis of Yongning; by rule it was reduced to baron.
translations.idiomatic: He first inherited Marquis of Yongning; by rule it fell to baron.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉李彪以道元執法清刻，自太傅掾引為書侍御史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, because Daoyuan in enforcing law was pure and severe, drew him from the Grand Tutor's staff as Secretary Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Biao, finding Daoyuan pure and severe in law, drew him from the Grand Tutor's staff as Secretary Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 彪為僕射李沖所奏，道元以屬官坐免。

translations.literal: When Biao was impeached by Vice Director Li Chong, Daoyuan as subordinate official was dismissed by association.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao was impeached by Vice Director Li Chong, Daoyuan as subordinate was dismissed with him.

sentences.zh: 景明中，為冀州鎮東府長史。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he was Chief Administrator of the Pacify-the-East office in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming he was Chief Administrator of the Pacify-the-East office in Ji.

sentences.zh: 刺史于勁，順皇后父也，西討關中，亦不至州，道元行事三年。

translations.literal: Inspector Yu Jin was father of the Shun empress; he campaigned west into Guanzhong and also did not reach the province—Daoyuan conducted affairs three years.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yu Jin was the Shun empress's father; campaigning west he never reached the province—Daoyuan ran affairs three years.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴酷，吏人畏之，奸盜逃於他境。

translations.literal: His government was harsh and cruel; officials and people feared him; thieves fled to other regions.
translations.idiomatic: Government was harsh; officials and people feared him; thieves fled elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 後試守魯陽郡，道元表立黌序，崇勸學教。

translations.literal: Later on probation he held Luoyang Commandery; Daoyuan memorialized to establish schools and honor and urge learning and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Later acting Administrator of Luoyang, he memorialized for schools and honored learning.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「魯陽本以蠻人，不立大學。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Luoyang was originally because of barbarians that no great academy was established.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Luoyang, being barbarian country, had no great academy.

sentences.zh: 今可聽之，以成良守文翁之化。

translations.literal: Now permission is granted, to complete the good administrator Wen Weng's transformation."
translations.idiomatic: Now it is permitted, to finish Wen Weng's transformation."

sentences.zh: 」道元在郡，山蠻伏其威名，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: In the commandery Daoyuan, the mountain barbarians submitted to his fierce name and did not dare raid.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery mountain tribes submitted to his name and did not raid.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，為東荊州刺史，威猛為政，如在冀州。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era he was Inspector of Eastern Jing; his fierce government was as in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang he was Eastern Jing Inspector; government was fierce as in Ji.

sentences.zh: 蠻人詣闕訟其刻峻，請前刺史寇祖禮。

translations.literal: The barbarians went to court to sue him for severity and asked for the former inspector Kou Zuli.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians sued at court for his harsh rule and asked for former inspector Kou Zuli.

sentences.zh: 及以遣戍兵七十人送道元還京，二人並坐免官。

translations.literal: When seventy garrison soldiers were sent to escort Daoyuan back to the capital, both men were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy garrison soldiers escorted Daoyuan to the capital; both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後為河南尹。

translations.literal: Later he was made Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 明帝以沃野、懷朔、薄骨律、武川、撫冥、柔玄、懷荒、禦夷諸鎮並改為州，其郡、縣、戍名，令准古城邑。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming changed the garrisons Woye, Huaishuo, Bogulv, Wuchuan, Fuming, Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Yuyi all to provinces, their commanderies, counties, and garrison names to follow ancient cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Ming turned garrisons Woye, Huaishuo, Bogulv, Wuchuan, Fuming, Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Yuyi into provinces, naming counties and posts after ancient towns.

sentences.zh: 詔道元持節兼黃門侍郎，馳驛與大都督李崇籌宜置立，裁減去留。

translations.literal: Daoyuan was ordered with staff as Concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant, traveling post-haste with Grand Commander Li Chong to plan establishment and cut or retain posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered Concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant to ride post-haste with Grand Commander Li Chong to plan posts and cuts.

sentences.zh: 會諸鎮叛，不果而還。

translations.literal: The garrisons rebelled; he returned without accomplishing it.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons rebelled; he returned without result.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，遣將攻揚州，刺史元法僧又于彭城反叛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang troops were sent to attack Yangzhou; Inspector Yuan Faseng also rebelled at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xiaochang troops attacked Yangzhou; Inspector Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔道元持節、兼侍中、攝行台尚書，節度諸軍，依僕射李平故事。

translations.literal: Daoyuan was ordered with staff, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and acting Mobile Secretariat Director to command the armies, following Vice Director Li Ping's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with staff, Concurrent Palace Attendant, acting Mobile Secretariat Director, commanding armies after Li Ping's precedent.

sentences.zh: 軍至渦陽，敗退。

translations.literal: The army reached Guoyang and was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Guoyang, was beaten, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 道元追討，多有斬獲。

translations.literal: Daoyuan pursued and beheaded many.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan pursued and took many heads.

sentences.zh: 後除御史中尉。

translations.literal: Later he was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 道元素有嚴猛之稱，權豪始頗憚之。

translations.literal: Daoyuan had always had the reputation of severity and fierceness; powerful families at first somewhat feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan had a name for severity; great houses at first feared him.

sentences.zh: 而不能有所糾正，聲望更損。

translations.literal: Yet he could not correct wrongs; his reputation fell further.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not correct abuses; his standing fell.

sentences.zh: 司州牧、汝南王悅嬖近左右丘念，常與臥起。

translations.literal: Governor of Si Province, Prince of Runan Yuan Yue, favored his intimate Qiu Nian, who constantly slept and rose with him.
translations.idiomatic: Si Governor, Prince of Runan Yuan Yue, favored Qiu Nian, who slept and rose with him.

sentences.zh: 及選州官，多由於念。

translations.literal: When choosing provincial officials, most came through Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing provincial officials mostly went through Nian.

sentences.zh: 念常匿悅第，時還其家，道元密訪知，收念付獄。

translations.literal: Nian often hid in Yue's residence and sometimes returned home; Daoyuan secretly learned of it and arrested Nian and put him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Nian hid in Yue's house and sometimes went home; Daoyuan learned secretly, arrested him, and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 悅啟靈太后，請全念身，有敕赦之。

translations.literal: Yue petitioned Empress Ling to spare Nian's life; there was an edict pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue petitioned Empress Ling to spare Nian; an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 道元遂盡其命，因以劾悅。

translations.literal: Daoyuan then took his life and therefore impeached Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan then executed him and impeached Yue.

sentences.zh: 時雍州刺史蕭寶夤反狀稍露，侍中、城陽王徽素忌道元，因諷朝廷，遣為關右大使。

translations.literal: At the time Inspector of Yong Xiao Baoyin's rebellion showed signs; Palace Attendant Prince of Chengyang Hui had long resented Daoyuan and therefore urged the court to send him as envoy to the west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Inspector Xiao Baoyin's revolt showed signs; Palace Attendant Prince of Chengyang Hui, resenting Daoyuan, urged sending him as envoy west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 寶夤慮道元圖己，遣其行台郎中郭子帙圍道元于陰盤驛亭。

translations.literal: Baoyin feared Daoyuan would plot against him and sent his mobile secretariat gentleman Guo Zixia to surround Daoyuan at Yinpan Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin feared Daoyuan and sent secretariat gentleman Guo Zixia to surround him at Yinpan Post.

sentences.zh: 亭在岡下，常食岡下之井。

translations.literal: The station lay below a hill; they regularly ate from the well below the hill.
translations.idiomatic: The post lay below a hill; they drank from the hill's well.

sentences.zh: 既被圍，穿井十餘丈不得水。

translations.literal: Once surrounded, they dug the well more than ten zhang and found no water.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged, they dug the well ten-plus zhang deep and found no water.

sentences.zh: 水盡力屈，賊遂逾牆而入。

translations.literal: Water gone and strength spent, the bandits climbed the wall and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Water gone, strength spent, rebels scaled the wall.

sentences.zh: 道元與其弟道闕二子俱被害。

translations.literal: Daoyuan, his younger brother Daolüe, and two sons were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan, younger brother Daolüe, and two sons were all killed.

sentences.zh: 道元瞋目叱賊，厲聲而死。

translations.literal: Daoyuan glared and shouted at the bandits, dying with a fierce voice.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan glared and cursed the rebels aloud, and died with his voice still fierce.

sentences.zh: 寶夤猶遣斂其父子，殯于長安城東。

translations.literal: Baoyin still sent men to gather father and sons and bury them east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin still sent men to bury father and sons east of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 事平，喪還，贈吏部尚書、冀州刺史、安定縣男。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled the coffin returned; he was posthumously made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Inspector of Ji, and Baron of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: When order returned the coffin came home; he was posthumously Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Ji Inspector, Baron of Anding.

translations.literal: The source text at this point is corrupt and unreadable.
translations.idiomatic: The source text at this point is corrupt and unreadable.

sentences.zh: 道元好學，曆覽奇書，撰注《水經》四十卷，《本志》十三篇。

translations.literal: Daoyuan loved learning, read through strange books, and wrote a commentary on the Water Classic in forty scrolls and Basic Records in thirteen sections.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan loved learning, read strange books, and wrote a commentary on the Water Classic in forty scrolls and Basic Records in thirteen sections.

sentences.zh: 又為《七聘》及諸文皆行於世。

translations.literal: He also wrote Seven Missions and other pieces, all current in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Seven Missions and other works, all current in the world.

sentences.zh: 然兄弟不能篤睦，又多嫌忌，時論薄之。

translations.literal: Yet the brothers could not live in harmony and were much given to suspicion; opinion of the time slighted them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the brothers were not harmonious and much suspicious; opinion slighted them.

sentences.zh: 子孝友襲。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoyou inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xiaoyou inherited.

sentences.zh: 道元第四弟道慎，字善季，涉歷史傳，有幹局。

translations.literal: Daoyuan's fourth younger brother Daoshen, styled Shanji, ranged through historical records and had administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth brother Daoshen, styled Shanji, ranged histories and had administrative gift.

sentences.zh: 位正平太守，有能名。

translations.literal: He held Administrator of Zhengping and had a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was Zhengping Administrator and had a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 遷長樂相。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He became Chancellor of Changle.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平州刺史。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Inspector of Ping.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Ping Inspector.

sentences.zh: 道慎弟道約，字善禮，樸質遲鈍，頗愛琴書。

translations.literal: Daoshen's younger brother Daoyue, styled Shanli, was plain and slow, and quite loved zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Daoyue, styled Shanli, was plain and slow, loving zither and books.

sentences.zh: 性多造請，好以榮利幹謁，乞丐不已，多為人所笑弄。

translations.literal: By nature he made many visits and liked to plead for glory and profit; begging without end, he was often laughed at.
translations.idiomatic: He made many calls and begged for rank and profit without end; men laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 坎壈於世，不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Hard pressed in the world, he could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed in the world, he could not escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 晚曆東萊、魯陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: Late in life he held the two commandery posts Donglai and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he held Donglai and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，吏人安之。

translations.literal: His government was quiet and pure; officials and people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Government was quiet; officials and people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 范弟道峻子惲，字幼和。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Daojun's son Yun, styled Youhe.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Daojun's son Yun, styled Youhe.

sentences.zh: 好學有文才，尤長吏幹。

translations.literal: Fond of learning, he had literary talent and especially excelled in administrative work.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, had literary gift, and excelled in administration.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，射策高第。

translations.literal: Presented as Outstanding Talent, he ranked high in the archery-and-policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: Presented as Outstanding Talent, he ranked high in archery and policy.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書外兵郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Outer Troops Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was Outer Troops Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 行台長孫承業引為行台郎。

translations.literal: Mobile Secretariat Chief Changsun Chengye drew him as secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Secretariat Chief Changsun Chengye made him secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 惲頗兼武用，恆以功名自許。

translations.literal: Yun also had martial gift and always aimed at merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Yun also had martial gift and aimed at merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 每進計於承業，多見納用。

translations.literal: Whenever he offered plans to Chengye, most were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Plans offered to Chengye were mostly adopted.

sentences.zh: 以功賞魏昌縣子。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was Viscount of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 惲在軍啟求減身官爵，為父請贈，詔授征虜將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: Yun at the army memorialized to reduce his own rank and title and ask posthumous grant for his father; the edict made his father General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of An.
translations.idiomatic: At the army Yun asked to cut his own rank for his father's posthumous grant; the edict made father General Who Punishes the Barbarians and An Inspector.

sentences.zh: 惲後與唐州刺史崔元珍固守平陽。

translations.literal: Later Yun with Tangzhou Inspector Cui Yuanzhen firmly held Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yun with Tangzhou Inspector Cui Yuanzhen held Pingyang firm.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮稱兵赴闕，惲與元珍不從，為榮行台郎中樊子鵠陷城，被害。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong raised troops to the capital; Yun and Yuanzhen would not follow and were killed when Rong's secretariat gentleman Fan Zigao took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong marched on the capital; Yun and Yuanzhen refused and were killed when Fan Zigao took the city.

sentences.zh: 所作文章，頗行於世。

translations.literal: Writings he composed circulated fairly widely.
translations.idiomatic: His writings circulated fairly widely.

sentences.zh: 撰慕容氏書，不成。

translations.literal: He drafted a book on the Murong house but did not finish.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a book on the Murong house but did not finish.

sentences.zh: 子懷則，司空長流參軍。

translations.literal: His son Huaize was Chief Clerk for flowing affairs in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Son Huaize was Chief Clerk for flowing affairs in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 韓秀，字白武，昌黎人也。

translations.literal: Han Xiu, styled Baiwu, was a man of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu, styled Baiwu, came from Changli.

sentences.zh: 祖宰，慕容俊謁者僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zai was Chamberlain for Attendants under Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Zai was Chamberlain for Attendants under Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 父景，皇始初歸魏，拜宣威將軍、騎都尉。

translations.literal: His father Jing, at the beginning of Huangshi, submitted to Wei and was made General Who Proclaims Might and Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Father Jing, at the start of Huangshi, submitted to Wei and was made General Who Proclaims Might and Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 秀歷位尚書郎，賜爵遂昌子。

translations.literal: Xiu held posts in the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed Viscount of Suichang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu served in the Masters of Writing and was Viscount of Suichang.

sentences.zh: 文成稱秀聰敏清辯，才任喉舌，遂命出納王言，並掌機密。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng called Xiu clever, clear in debate, and fit for the throat and tongue; he therefore ordered him to issue and receive the king's words and also handle secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng called Xiu clever and clear in debate, fit for the king's voice; he issued and received words and handled secrets.

sentences.zh: 行幸遊獵，隨侍左右。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses and hunts he attended at the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: On progresses and hunts he attended left and right.

sentences.zh: 獻文即位，轉給事中，參征南慕容白曜軍事。

translations.literal: When Xianwen took the throne he was transferred to Palace Attendant and joined the staff of Grand General of the South Murong Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianwen took the throne he was Palace Attendant on Baiyao's southern staff.

sentences.zh: 延興中，尚書奏以敦煌一鎮，介遠西北，寇賊路沖，慮或不固，欲移就涼州。

translations.literal: In the Yansing era the Masters of Writing memorialized that Dunhuang, one garrison, lay far in the northwest on the bandit route and might not hold, and wished to move it to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yansing the Masters of Writing said Dunhuang lay far northwest on the bandit road and might not hold, and wished to move it to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 群臣會議，僉以為然。

translations.literal: The ministers met in council; all thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers met; all agreed.

sentences.zh: 秀獨曰：「此蹙國之事，非辟土之宜。

translations.literal: Xiu alone said: "This is a matter of shrinking the state, not of opening territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu alone said, "This shrinks the state; it is not opening territory.

sentences.zh: 愚謂敦煌之立，其來已久，雖鄰強寇，而兵人素習，循常置戍，足以自全。

translations.literal: I hold that Dunhuang was established long ago; though neighboring strong bandits, soldiers and people are used to it—routine garrison placement is enough for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Dunhuang was long established; though bandits neighbor it, soldiers and people are used to routine garrison—enough for defense.

sentences.zh: 若徙就姑臧，慮人懷異意，或貪留重遷，情不願徙。

translations.literal: If moved to Guzang, I fear men will harbor other thoughts, or greed for what they leave in heavy relocation and be unwilling to move.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Guzang, men may harbor other thoughts, or cling to what they leave and refuse to go.

sentences.zh: 脫引寇內侵，深為國患。

translations.literal: If bandits are thereby drawn to invade within, it will deeply harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: If that draws bandits inward, the state is deeply harmed.

sentences.zh: 且舍遠就近，遙防有闕。

translations.literal: Moreover, abandoning the far for the near leaves distant defense gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning the far for the near leaves distant defense gaps.

sentences.zh: 一旦廢罷，是啟戎心，則夷狄交構，互相來往。

translations.literal: Once abolished, that awakens the barbarians' hearts; then Yi and Di will intrigue and come and go with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Once abolished, barbarian hearts awaken; Yi and Di intrigue and pass back and forth.

sentences.zh: 關右荒擾，烽警不息，邊役煩興，艱難方甚。

translations.literal: Guanxi will be disturbed in the wild; beacon alarms will not cease; frontier service will multiply and hardship will be great.
translations.idiomatic: Guanxi will run wild; beacons will not cease; frontier service will multiply and hardship grow.

sentences.zh: 」乃從秀議。

translations.literal: "They followed Xiu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Xiu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 後為平東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was General Who Pacifies the East and Qing Inspector.

sentences.zh: 卒，子務襲爵。

translations.literal: At death his son Wu inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: At death son Wu inherited.

sentences.zh: 務字道世，性端謹，有吏幹。

translations.literal: Wu, styled Daoshi, was upright and careful and had administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, styled Daoshi, was upright, careful, and capable in administration.

sentences.zh: 為定州平北長史，頗有受納，為御史中尉李平所劾。

translations.literal: As Chief Administrator of Pacify-the-North in Dingzhou he took many bribes and was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Li Ping.
translations.idiomatic: As Dingzhou Pacify-the-North Chief Administrator he took bribes and was impeached by Censor Li Ping.

sentences.zh: 付廷尉，會赦免。

translations.literal: Handed to the Court of Justice, he was pardoned when an amnesty came.
translations.idiomatic: Handed to the Court of Justice, he was freed by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 後除龍驤將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made Dragon-Prancing General and Inspector of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Dragon-Prancing General and Ying Inspector.

sentences.zh: 務獻七寶床、象牙席。

translations.literal: Wu presented a bed of seven treasures and an ivory mat.
translations.idiomatic: Wu presented a seven-treasure bed and ivory mat.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔晉武帝焚雉頭裘，朕常嘉之。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Formerly Jin Emperor Wu burned the pheasant-head robe; I have always praised that.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Jin Emperor Wu burned the pheasant-head robe; I have always praised that.

sentences.zh: 今務所獻，亦此之流也。

translations.literal: What Wu now presents is also of that sort.
translations.idiomatic: What Wu presents is of that sort.

sentences.zh: 奇麗之物，有乖風素，可付其家人。

translations.literal: Curious and gorgeous things violate plain custom; give them to his household people."
translations.idiomatic: Gorgeous things violate plain custom; give them to his household."

sentences.zh: 」後以詐表破賊，免官。

translations.literal: Later for falsely reporting defeating bandits he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later for falsely reporting bandit victories he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜太中大夫，進號左將軍，卒。

translations.literal: After long time he was made Grand Master of Palace Counsel and advanced to General of the Left; he died.
translations.idiomatic: After long time he was Grand Master of Palace Counsel and General of the Left; he died.

sentences.zh: 堯暄，字辟邪，上党長子人也。

translations.literal: Yao Xuan, styled Bixie, was a man of Changzi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan, styled Bixie, came from Changzi in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 本名鐘葵，後賜名暄。

translations.literal: His original name was Zhongkui; later he was granted the name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Zhongkui; later he was granted the name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 祖僧賴，道武平中山，與趙郡呂含首來歸國。

translations.literal: His grandfather Senglai, when Daowu pacified Zhongshan, came to submit to the state with Lü Han of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Senglai, when Daowu pacified Zhongshan, came to submit with Lü Han of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 暄聰了，美容貌。

translations.literal: Xuan was clever and had a beautiful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was clever and handsome.

sentences.zh: 為千人軍將。

translations.literal: He was commander of a thousand-man army.
translations.idiomatic: He was commander of a thousand-man army.

sentences.zh: 太武以其恭謹，擢為中散。

translations.literal: Taiwu for his respectful care promoted him to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu for respectful care promoted him to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後兼北部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was also Director of the Northern Department in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was also Northern Department Director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 于時始立三長，暄為東道十三州使，更比戶籍，賜獨車一乘，廄馬四匹。

translations.literal: At the time the Three Chiefs were first established; Xuan was envoy to the thirteen eastern provinces to revise household registers and was granted one private carriage and four stable horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Chiefs were first established, Xuan was envoy to thirteen eastern provinces to revise registers and was granted a carriage and four stable horses.

sentences.zh: 暄前後從征及出使檢案三十許度，皆有克己奉公之稱。

translations.literal: Xuan before and after followed campaigns and went out on inspection some thirty times, all with a name for restraining self and serving the public.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he followed campaigns and inspected some thirty times, all with a name for self-restraint and public service.

sentences.zh: 賞賜衣服、彩絹、奴婢等物，賜爵平陽伯。

translations.literal: Rewards of clothes, colored silk, and slave girls and the like; he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded with clothes, silk, and slaves, he was Baron of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 及改置百官，授太僕卿，轉大司農。

translations.literal: When the hundred offices were reorganized he was made Minister of the Imperial Stud and transferred to Minister of Grain.
translations.idiomatic: When offices were reorganized he was Minister of the Imperial Stud, then Minister of Grain.

sentences.zh: 卒于平城。

translations.literal: He died at Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 孝文為之舉哀，贈相州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiaowen mourned him and posthumously made him Inspector of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen mourned him and posthumously made him Xiang Inspector.

sentences.zh: 初，暄至徐州，見州城樓觀，嫌其華盛，乃令往往毀徹，由是，後更損落。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuan reached Xuzhou and saw the commandery towers and belvederes, he disliked their splendor and ordered them torn down here and there; therefore they later fell further into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at Xuzhou he disliked the towers' splendor and had them torn down; they fell further into ruin.

sentences.zh: 及孝文幸彭城，聞之，曰：「暄猶可追斬。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen visited Pengcheng and heard of it, he said: "Xuan could still be pursued and beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen visited Pengcheng he said, "Xuan could still be pursued and beheaded."

sentences.zh: 」暄長子洪襲爵。

translations.literal: Xuan's eldest son Hong inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Hong inherited.

sentences.zh: 洪子傑，字永壽。

translations.literal: Hong's son Jie, styled Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Jie, styled Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 元象中，開府儀同三司、樂城縣公。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of the same rites as the Three Dukes and Duke of Lecheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Three-Duke rites and Duke of Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 洪弟遵，位臨洮太守。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Zun held Administrator of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zun was Lintao Administrator.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰思。

translations.literal: At death posthumous name Si.
translations.idiomatic: At death posthumous name Si.

sentences.zh: 遵弟榮，位員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Zun's younger brother Rong held Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Rong was Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子雄，字休武，少驍果，輕財重氣。

translations.literal: His son Xiong, styled Xiuwu, in youth was brave and decisive, light with wealth and heavy with spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xiong, styled Xiuwu, was young, brave, light with wealth, heavy with spirit.

sentences.zh: 位燕州刺史、平城縣伯。

translations.literal: He held Inspector of Yan and Baron of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was Yan Inspector and Baron of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 隨爾硃兆與齊神武戰，敗于廣阿，率所部據定州歸神武。

translations.literal: Following Erzhu Zhao in battle with Qi Shenwu, defeated at Guang'a, he led his command and held Dingzhou, submitting to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Following Erzhu Zhao against Qi Shenwu, beaten at Guang'a, he held Dingzhou and submitted to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 其從兄傑為兆滄州刺史，亦遣使降。

translations.literal: His older cousin Jie was Zhao's Cangzhou inspector; he also sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Jie was Zhao's Cangzhou inspector; he too sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 神武以其兄弟俱有誠款，使傑便為行瀛州事。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because the brothers both showed sincere intent, had Jie act as acting Yingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu, seeing sincere intent in both brothers, had Jie act for Ying.

sentences.zh: 使雄代傑為瀛州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He had Xiong replace Jie as Ying Inspector and advanced his rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xiong replace Jie as Ying Inspector and advanced him to duke.

sentences.zh: 時禁網疏闊，官司相與聚斂。

translations.literal: At the time the prohibition net was loose; officials mutually amassed wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The prohibition net was loose; officials amassed wealth together.

sentences.zh: 唯雄義然後取，接下以恩，甚為吏人所懷。

translations.literal: Only Xiong took after righteousness; he treated subordinates with kindness and was much cherished by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiong took after righteousness; he treated subordinates kindly and was cherished.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武帝入關，雄為大都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei entered the Pass, Xiong was Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Xiaowu entered the Pass, Xiong was Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 隨高昂破賀拔勝於穰城，仍除豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Following Gao Anguo he broke Heba Sheng at Rangcheng and was then made Inspector of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Following Gao Anguo he broke Heba Sheng at Rang and was made Yu Inspector.

sentences.zh: 元洪威據潁川叛。

translations.literal: Yuan Hongwei held Yingchuan in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongwei rebelled holding Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 叛人趙繼宗殺潁川太守邵招，據樂口，北應洪威。

translations.literal: The rebel Zhao Jizong killed Yingchuan Administrator Shao Zhao, held Lekou, and answered Hongwei in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Zhao Jizong killed Yingchuan Administrator Shao Zhao, held Lekou, and answered Hongwei from the north.

sentences.zh: 雄討之，繼宗敗走。

translations.literal: Xiong attacked; Jizong was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong attacked; Jizong was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 城內因雄之出，據州引西魏。

translations.literal: Within the city, because Xiong had gone out, they seized the province and called in Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiong was out the city seized the province and called in Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 雄復與行台侯景討平之。

translations.literal: Xiong again with Mobile Secretariat Hou Jing pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong again with Hou Jing pacified it.

sentences.zh: 梁將李洪芝、王當伯襲破平鄉城，雄並禽之。

translations.literal: Liang generals Li Hongzhi and Wang Dangbo stormed and took Pingxiang; Xiong captured them both.
translations.idiomatic: Liang generals Li Hongzhi and Wang Dangbo took Pingxiang; Xiong captured both.

sentences.zh: 又破梁司州刺史陳慶之，復圍南荊州。

translations.literal: He also broke Liang Inspector of Si Chen Qingzhi and again besieged Southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Liang Si Inspector Chen Qingzhi and again besieged Southern Jing.

sentences.zh: 東救未至，雄陷其城。

translations.literal: Eastern rescue had not arrived; Xiong took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern rescue had not come; Xiong took the city.

sentences.zh: 梁以元慶和為魏王，侵擾南境。

translations.literal: Liang made Yuan Qinghe Prince of Wei to harass the southern border.
translations.idiomatic: Liang made Yuan Qinghe Prince of Wei to harass the south.

sentences.zh: 雄大破之于南頓。

translations.literal: Xiong greatly defeated him at Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong greatly defeated him at Nandun.

sentences.zh: 尋與行台侯景破梁楚城。

translations.literal: Soon he with Mobile Secretariat Hou Jing took Liang's Chucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon with Hou Jing he took Liang's Chucheng.

sentences.zh: 豫州人上書，更乞雄為刺史，復行豫州事。

translations.literal: Men of Yu province memorialized, again asking for Xiong as inspector; he again conducted Yu affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu men memorialized again for Xiong as inspector; he again ran Yu.

sentences.zh: 潁州長史賀若統執刺史田迅，據州降西魏。

translations.literal: Yingzhou Chief Administrator He Ruo seized Inspector Tian Xun, held the province, and surrendered to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Chief Administrator He Ruo seized Inspector Tian Xun, held the province, and surrendered to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 詔雄與廣州刺史趙育、揚州刺史是寶，隨行台任祥攻之。

translations.literal: The edict ordered Xiong with Guangzhou Inspector Zhao Yu and Yangzhou Inspector Shi Bao to follow Mobile Secretariat Ren Xiang in attacking.
translations.idiomatic: The edict ordered Xiong with Zhao Yu of Guangzhou and Shi Bao of Yangzhou to follow Ren Xiang in attack.

sentences.zh: 西魏將怡鋒敗祥等，育、寶各還，據城降敵。

translations.literal: Western Wei general Yi Feng defeated Xiang and the rest; Yu and Bao each returned and held their cities, surrendering to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei general Yi Feng beat Xiang; Yu and Bao returned to their cities and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 雄收散卒，保大梁。

translations.literal: Xiong gathered scattered troops and held Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong gathered scattered troops and held Daliang.

sentences.zh: 周文帝遣其右丞韋孝寬等攻豫州，雄都督程多寶降之。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Wen sent his Vice Director Wei Xiaokuan and others to attack Yu; Xiong's commander Cheng Duobao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen sent Vice Director Wei Xiaokuan to attack Yu; commander Cheng Duobao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 執刺史馮邕，並雄家屬及部下妻子數千口，欲送長安。

translations.literal: They seized Inspector Feng Yong and with Xiong's household and subordinates' wives numbering thousands intended to send them to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Inspector Feng Yong and Xiong's household and subordinates' wives by the thousands, bound for Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 至樂口，友外兵參軍王恆伽、都督赫連俊等從大梁邀之。

translations.literal: At Lekou, friend Outer Troops Staff Officer Wang Hengjia and commander Helian Jun and others intercepted from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: At Lekou, staff officer Wang Hengjia and commander Helian Jun intercepted from Daliang.

sentences.zh: 斬多寶，收雄家口還大梁。

translations.literal: They beheaded Duobao and brought Xiong's household back to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: They beheaded Duobao and brought Xiong's household back to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 雄別破樂口，禽丞伯，進討縣瓠。

translations.literal: Xiong separately broke Lekou, captured Cheng Bo, and advanced to attack Xianhu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong separately broke Lekou, captured Cheng Bo, and advanced on Xianhu.

sentences.zh: 復以雄行豫州事。

translations.literal: Again Xiong was made acting Inspector of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was acting Yu Inspector.

sentences.zh: 西魏以是寶為揚州刺史，據項城，義州刺史韓顯據南頓。

translations.literal: Western Wei made Shi Bao Yangzhou inspector, holding Xiangcheng; Yi Inspector Han Xian held Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Shi Bao Yangzhou inspector at Xiangcheng; Yi Inspector Han Xian held Nandun.

sentences.zh: 雄一日拔其二城，禽顯及長史嶽，寶遁走。

translations.literal: In one day Xiong took both cities, captured Xian and Chief Administrator Yue; Bao fled.
translations.idiomatic: In one day he took both cities, captured Xian and Chief Administrator Yue; Bao fled.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，仍隨侯景平魯陽，復除豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of the same rites as the Three Dukes, still followed Hou Jing in pacifying Luoyang, and again was made Inspector of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Three-Duke rites, followed Hou Jing to pacify Luoyang, and again was Yu Inspector.

sentences.zh: 雄雖武將，性質寬厚，為政舉其大綱而已。

translations.literal: Though Xiong was a martial man, his nature was generous and thick; in government he took only the great outline.
translations.idiomatic: Though a martial man, Xiong was generous; in government he kept only the great outline.

sentences.zh: 在邊十年，屢有功績。

translations.literal: On the frontier ten years he repeatedly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years on the frontier brought repeated merit.

sentences.zh: 愛人物，多所施與，亦以此稱。

translations.literal: He loved people and gave much away; he was also praised for this.
translations.idiomatic: He loved people and gave much away; he was praised for that too.

sentences.zh: 興和四年，卒於鄴，贈司徒，諡曰武恭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xinghe he died at Ye; posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous name Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe year four he died at Ye; posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous name Wugong.

sentences.zh: 子師嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shi inherited.

sentences.zh: 柳崇，字僧生，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Chong, styled Sengsheng, was a man of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong, styled Sengsheng, came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 七世祖軌，晉廷尉卿。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Gui was Jin Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh-generation ancestor Gui was Jin Director of Justice.

sentences.zh: 崇方雅有器量，身長八尺，美須明目，兼有學行。

translations.literal: Chong was refined and had capacity; eight feet tall, beautiful beard and bright eyes, and together had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was refined and capable, eight feet tall, fine beard and bright eyes, with learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，射策高第。

translations.literal: Presented as Outstanding Talent, he ranked high in the archery-and-policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: Presented as Outstanding Talent, he ranked high in archery and policy.

sentences.zh: 解褐太尉主簿，轉尚書右外兵郎中。

translations.literal: On leaving the sack he was Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister; transferred to Outer Troops Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving the sack he was Grand Minister Chief Clerk; transferred to Outer Troops Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 于時河東、河北二郡爭境。

translations.literal: At the time Hedong and Hebei commanderies disputed the border.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong and Hebei disputed the border.

sentences.zh: 其間有鹽池之饒，虞阪之便，守宰百姓皆恐外割；

translations.literal: Between them were rich salt pools and the convenience of Yufan Pass; magistrates and common people all feared outside partition.
translations.idiomatic: Between them lay rich salt pools and Yufan Pass; magistrates and people feared partition.

sentences.zh: 公私朋競，紛囂台府。

translations.literal: Public and private factions competed; clamor filled the central offices.
translations.idiomatic: Factions competed; clamor filled the central offices.

sentences.zh: 孝文乃遣崇檢斷，上下息訟。

translations.literal: Xiaowen therefore sent Chong to inspect and decide; above and below the lawsuits ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen sent Chong to inspect and decide; lawsuits ceased above and below.

sentences.zh: 屬荊、郢新附，南寇窺擾，又詔崇持節與州郡經略，加慰喻。

translations.literal: As Jing and Ying were newly submitted and southern bandits watched for trouble, Chong was again ordered with staff to plan with provinces and commanderies and add comfort and persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: As Jing and Ying were newly submitted and southern bandits watched, Chong was again ordered with staff to plan with provinces and add comfort.

sentences.zh: 還，遷太子洗馬、本郡中正。

translations.literal: On return he was made Mentor to the Heir Apparent and chief rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was Heir Apparent Mentor and native commandery chief rectifier.

sentences.zh: 累遷河中太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Administrator of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Hezhong Administrator.

sentences.zh: 崇初屈郡，郡人張明失馬，疑執十餘人。

translations.literal: When Chong first took the commandery, a man of the commandery named Zhang Ming lost a horse and suspected and seized more than ten people.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong first took office, Zhang Ming lost a horse and seized more than ten suspects.

sentences.zh: 崇見之，不問賊事，人別藉以溫顏，更問其親老存不，農業多少，而微察其辭色。

translations.literal: Chong saw them, did not ask about the bandit affair, but to each separately gave a warm countenance and instead asked whether their parents and elders still lived and how much agriculture they had, while subtly observing their words and color.
translations.idiomatic: Chong saw them, asked nothing of the theft, gave each a warm face, asked after parents and harvest, and watched their color.

sentences.zh: 即獲真賊呂穆等二人，餘皆放遣。

translations.literal: He immediately obtained the true bandits Lü Mu and two others; the rest were all released.
translations.idiomatic: He at once had the true thieves, Lü Mu and one other; the rest were released.

sentences.zh: 郡中畏服，境內怗然。

translations.literal: Within the commandery they submitted in awe; within the borders all was calm.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery submitted in awe; the borders were calm.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，贈岐州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously made Inspector of Qi, posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumously Qi Inspector, posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 崇所制文章，寇亂遺失。

translations.literal: Writings Chong composed were lost in the turmoil of invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Writings he composed were lost in invasion.

sentences.zh: 長子慶和，性沉靜，不競于時。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qinghe was by nature calm and did not compete in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Qinghe was calm and did not compete in the age.

sentences.zh: 位給事中、本郡中正，卒。

translations.literal: He held Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of his native commandery; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was Palace Attendant and native chief rectifier; he died.

sentences.zh: 慶和弟楷，字士則。

translations.literal: Qinghe's younger brother Kai, styled Shize.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Kai, styled Shize.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，善草書，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: Eight feet tall, skilled in cursive script, he ranged fairly widely through literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet tall, skilled in cursive script, he ranged through literature and history.

sentences.zh: 位撫軍司馬。

translations.literal: He held Marshal of the Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was Marshal of the Pacification Army.

sentences.zh: 論曰：屈遵學知機。

translations.literal: Commentary: Qun Zun in learning knew the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Qun Zun's learning knew the turning of affairs.

sentences.zh: 恆乃局量受委。

translations.literal: Heng then had measure to receive commission.
translations.idiomatic: Heng had the measure to bear great trust.

sentences.zh: 張蒲、谷渾，文武為用，人世仍顯，不亦善乎？

translations.literal: Zhang Pu and Gu Hun—civil and martial both used—their houses still shine through generations; is that not good?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu and Gu Hun, civil gift and martial both employed—their houses still shine through generations; is that not well?

sentences.zh: 公孫表初則一介見知，終以輕薄致戾。

translations.literal: Gong Sunbiao at first was known from a single encounter; in the end he met blame through lightness.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sunbiao was first known from a single meeting; in the end lightness brought ruin.

sentences.zh: 軌始受探金之賞，末陷財利之嫌，鮮克有終，固不虛也。

translations.literal: Gui first received the reward of probing gold; in the end he fell under suspicion of wealth—few keep their end to the end; it is not empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: Gui first won the reward of gold probed from the vault; in the end he fell under wealth's suspicion—few keep their end; the proverb is not empty.

sentences.zh: 張濟使于四方，有延譽之美。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji as envoy to the four directions had the beauty of extending reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, envoy to the four directions, had the gift of extending a man's name.

sentences.zh: 李先學術嘉謀，荷遇三世。

translations.literal: Li Xian in learning and counsel was excellent and bore favor through three reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian excelled in learning and counsel and bore favor through three reigns.

sentences.zh: 賈彝早播時譽。

translations.literal: Jia Yi early spread the reputation of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi early spread his name through the age.

sentences.zh: 秀則不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Xiu then did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu then did not fear the powerful.

sentences.zh: 竇瑾、李䐶，時曰良幹。

translations.literal: Dou Jin and Li Xin—men of the time called them able pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin and Li Xin—men of the time called them able pillars of state.

sentences.zh: 瑾以片言疑似，䐶以夙故猜嫌，而嬰合門之戮，良可悲也。

translations.literal: Jin for a phrase of suspicion, Xin for old grudge and suspicion—yet both met slaughter of the whole gate; truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Jin for a phrase held suspicious, Xin for an old grudge held in suspicion—yet both met slaughter of the whole gate; pitiable indeed.

sentences.zh: 韓延之忠於所事，有國士之烈。

translations.literal: Han Yanzhi was loyal to what he served and had the fierceness of a champion of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi was loyal to his lord and had the fierceness of a champion of the state.

sentences.zh: 袁式取遇崔公，以博雅而重。

translations.literal: Yuan Shi won meeting with Lord Cui and was heavy for breadth and elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shi won meeting with Lord Cui and was esteemed for breadth and elegance.

sentences.zh: 脩之晚著誠款。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi late showed sincere intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi in late years showed sincere intent.

sentences.zh: 唐和萬里慕義。

translations.literal: Tang He for ten thousand li admired righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He, ten thousand li from home, admired righteousness.

sentences.zh: 寇贊誠信見嘉。

translations.literal: Kou Zan in sincerity and faith was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zan in sincerity and faith won praise.

sentences.zh: 酈范智器而達。

translations.literal: Li Fan had wise vessels and reached through.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan had wise capacity and saw his way through.

sentences.zh: 道元遭命，有銜須之風。

translations.literal: Daoyuan met his doom and had the spirit of one who sets his teeth in his beard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoyuan met his doom with the spirit of a man who sets his teeth in his beard.

sentences.zh: 韓秀議邊，得馭遠之算。

translations.literal: Han Xiu in debating the frontier had the calculation to control the far.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu, debating the frontier, had the calculation to hold the far.

sentences.zh: 堯暄聰察致位，禮加存沒。

translations.literal: Yao Xuan by clever observation rose to rank; rites were added in life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan rose by keen observation; rites followed him in life and death.

sentences.zh: 構崇素業有資，器行仍世。

translations.literal: Liu Chong's plain achievement had substance; vessel and conduct lasted through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong's plain learning had substance; character and conduct ran through generations.

sentences.zh: 盛矣乎！

translations.literal: How magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Magnificent indeed!
